findings.description: MindControlled.wear_off_duration is hardcoded to the magic literal 300.0 in martina_mind_control. There is no named constant, no explanation of why Martina's duration differs from wizard-cast values, and the value is indistinguishable from 'permanent'.
findings.recommendation: Extract to a named constant MARTINA_MIND_CONTROL_DURATION in constants.rs with a comment explaining the design intent.

findings.description: cleanse_fear_with_rage and update_fear_movement are cross-cutting units-level systems (FearModifier is defined and ticked in units/status_effects.rs + units/plugin.rs). They are stranded in movement.rs only because Ray is the only current fear source.
findings.recommendation: Move both systems to src/game/units/status_effects.rs or a dedicated units/fear.rs and register them in units/plugin.rs alongside the existing FearModifier tick.

findings.description: The has_targets range check (any defender within MAX_BEAM_RANGE?) is inlined identically in at least three beam attack functions: disintegration (movement.rs:710), petrification (movement.rs:942), and mind control (beams.rs:82).
findings.recommendation: Extract any_defender_in_range(boss_pos, defenders, team_query, max_range) into beams.rs helpers or boss/utils.rs and call it from each beam system.

findings.description: The four-line doc comment '/// Scales a font size down based on text width…' is pasted directly above `apply_parchment_backgrounds`. The function it describes (`scale_font_by_text_width`) exists only in button_systems.rs. Any reader of layout_helpers.rs will be misled about what apply_parchment_backgrounds does.
findings.recommendation: Delete lines 32–35 (the misplaced doc block) and write a correct doc comment for apply_parchment_backgrounds in its place.

findings.description: spawn_controls_tab calls crate::config::save_data::load_unified_save() (synchronous disk I/O) every time the Controls tab is rebuilt. Tab rebuilds happen on every Controls tab activation, including switching away and back. This performs a full save-file deserialize on each tab switch.
findings.recommendation: Cache the unlocked wizard types in a Resource loaded once at startup (or read from the already-loaded SaveData resource if it exists) and pass it as a system parameter instead of re-reading the save file on each tab rebuild.

findings.description: load_unified_save() (full filesystem read + TOML parse) is called every time CompendiumState::is_changed() is true inside rebuild_on_state_change. This fires on every tab switch AND every item click.
findings.recommendation: Cache loaded save data in CompendiumState on resource insertion, refreshing only after actual mutations (toggle_save_run writes back to disk). Pass the cached data through instead of re-reading disk.

findings.description: Per-target sqrt() called inside the innermost filter_map on every attacker×target pair. Only the minimum distance is needed; the absolute value is never used downstream after target selection.
findings.recommendation: Compare squared distances in the filter_map (promote attack_range to squared too). Reserve sqrt only for the one accepted target if the raw distance is ever needed, reducing O(n*m) sqrt calls to at most one per attacker per frame.

findings.description: emit_impact_particles (lines 396-401) and emit_beam_smoke (lines 498-503) independently compute an identical 5-line perpendicular basis: up = if direction.y.abs() > 0.9 { Vec3::X } else { Vec3::Y }; right = direction.cross(up).normalize(); forward = right.cross(direction).normalize(). These are the two most frequently called VFX helpers in the module.
findings.recommendation: Extract fn perp_basis(direction: Vec3) -> (Vec3, Vec3) returning (right, forward) and call it from both sites.

findings.description: Two teleport-completion branches (early-release at line 530 and timer-complete at line 635) duplicate ~40 lines each: execute_teleport call, result field assignment, and Lingering Gate bookkeeping. They differ only in radius expression and whether the source gets a contracting vs non-contracting aura bubble.
findings.recommendation: Extract a fn finalize_teleport(...) helper that takes source_pos, dest_pos, radius, contracting: bool and fills the TeleportCastResult.

findings.description: TeleportDestinationCircle::pulse_scale (lines 60-64) and TeleportSourceCircle::pulse_scale (lines 89-93) are byte-for-byte identical: same constants, same formula, same pulse_freq and pulse_amplitude magic numbers.
findings.recommendation: Extract fn pulse_scale_for(time_alive: f32) -> f32 as a module-private helper and call it from both impl blocks.

findings.description: TeleportTalentParams.disorienting_arrival doc says 'stun enemies, haste allies on arrival.' The implementation in arrival.rs:279-288 inserts Stunned on ALL teleported entities with no team filter. constants.rs:42 also says 'stun enemies.' The doc contradicts the code.
findings.recommendation: Fix the doc to say 'stun all teleported units (friendly fire applies)' to match actual behaviour, or add a team filter if selective stun was intended.

findings.description: `spawn_wall_dust` accepts `sinking_walls: Query<&WallOfStone, Without<WallRising>>` then filters `if wall.sinking` in the loop body. Every non-rising wall (the full standing population) is visited every dust-interval tick for no effect.
findings.recommendation: Add a `SinkingWall` marker component so the query can be `Query<&WallOfStone, With<SinkingWall>>`, eliminating the dead scan over all standing walls.

findings.description: `maze_architect_bonus` iterates all `WallOfStone` entities twice per frame (once to count + detect `has_maze`, once to apply HP). Runs every frame under `any_with_component::<WallTalents>()` which is true whenever any wall exists.
findings.recommendation: Cache bonus-active state in a Resource updated only when wall count changes, or merge the two passes into one by collecting data and applying in a single iteration.

findings.description: apply_grease_slow — a passive zone-effect tick system including Slip and Fall stun application and Oil Slick vulnerability management — lives in casting.rs alongside input-driven casting logic. It has no dependency on casting inputs. This is naming drift: casting.rs implies input-handling code but also contains a core gameplay tick system (124 lines).
findings.recommendation: Move apply_grease_slow to a new slow.rs, or into lifecycle.rs when G-02 is addressed. Update the systems.rs re-export shim.

findings.description: ChainLightningCooldown::new() initializes time_remaining to 2.0, FireballCooldown::new() to 5.0, and TeleportPullCooldown::new() to 6.0, but the corresponding cycle constants are CHAIN_LIGHTNING_COOLDOWN=1.0, FIREBALL_COOLDOWN=2.0, and TELEPORT_PULL_COOLDOWN=2.0 respectively. The initial values silently diverge from the gameplay cadence with no documentation explaining whether this is an intentional startup delay or unintended drift.
findings.recommendation: Introduce named constants CHAIN_LIGHTNING_INITIAL_COOLDOWN, FIREBALL_INITIAL_COOLDOWN, TELEPORT_PULL_INITIAL_COOLDOWN (or reuse existing constants) and add a doc comment clarifying the startup-delay intent.

findings.description: spawn_dark_mage lives in ai.rs alongside movement, spell-queue, AI state machine, and teleport logic making ai.rs 587 LOC. Every other boss (lich, ogre) isolates spawn in a dedicated spawn.rs.
findings.recommendation: Extract spawn_dark_mage and its direct imports into a new spawn.rs sibling. Consider also extracting dark_mage_teleport into teleport.rs to reduce ai.rs to ~300 LOC.

findings.description: calculate_weighted_movement and is_cc_immobilized are called with full crate-path qualifiers (crate::game::units::systems::) at lines 156, 274, and 478. Stunned and Petrified are also referenced by full path at lines 245-246 and 444-445. Other boss files use top-of-file imports.
findings.recommendation: Add use crate::game::units::systems::{calculate_weighted_movement, is_cc_immobilized}; and use crate::game::units::components::{MeleeDamageReduction, Stunned, Petrified}; to the ai.rs import block.

findings.description: dispeller_tick_dispel_channel, dispeller_refresh_casting_animation, and dispeller_spawn_channel_particles are gated with any_with_component::<ChannelingCast> — a global check that fires whenever any entity (healer, wizard, etc.) is channeling. The same bug exists in shielder/plugin.rs:31. This wakes 6 systems every frame a healer channels, all of which then iterate over 0 dispeller/shielder entities.
findings.recommendation: Change the guard to any_exist::<Dispeller>().and(any_with_component::<ChannelingCast>) for the dispeller group, and the analogous compound for shielder.

findings.description: Ingredient unlock checks use format!("{:?}", i) (Rust Debug format) to produce the save-data key string. If an Ingredient variant is ever renamed, or a custom Debug impl is added, saved unlock data silently becomes inconsistent with no compile-time signal. The same pattern appears in interaction.rs:247 (combo name matching) and is widespread in the compendium.
findings.recommendation: Add a fn save_key(&self) -> &'static str method to Ingredient (and combos) that returns an explicit stable string independent of the variant name or Debug impl. Use it everywhere an enum variant is serialized as a string key.

findings.description: plugin.rs contains two non-trivial Bevy system bodies: handle_main_menu_back_button and handle_pause_menu_back_button. Project convention is plugin.rs for registration only; system bodies belong in systems.rs.
findings.recommendation: Move both handlers into systems.rs as pub(super) functions, then reference them from plugin.rs.

findings.description: check_master_brewer, check_grand_council (line 1011), and check_walking_library (line 1032) each call load_unified_save() and silently fall back to defaults on failure via unwrap_or_default / unwrap_or(0). If the save file is temporarily unreadable on Windows (file lock), the achievement silently fails to unlock with no log output.
findings.recommendation: Add a warn!() log on save-read failure so missed unlocks are observable in production logs. Long-term, pass the relevant counts through the triggering message to avoid repeated disk reads per event.

findings.description: check_shielder_encounter, check_assassin_encounter, and check_aerialist_encounter use a Local<bool> self-latch instead of the achievement_locked run_if guard used by all other encounter systems. They run every gameplay frame until the Local<bool> is set — inconsistent with the rest of the pattern and not disabled at the plugin scheduling level.
findings.recommendation: Add dedicated resource types for these three encounters so they can use achievement_locked guards in plugin.rs, matching the established encounter_system! pattern. If truly 'unit-unlock only, no achievement', document this distinction explicitly in the macro.

findings.description: Multiple duplicate talent names exist across spells: 'Chain Reaction' appears in electric.rs at lines 56 and 97 (different spells); 'Magnetic Pull' in electric.rs:41 and force.rs:97; 'Scorched Earth' in fire.rs:56 and fire.rs:171; 'Lingering Flames' in fire.rs:14 and nature.rs:313; 'Dimensional Rift' in force.rs:198 and utility.rs:322. Duplicate names across different spells risk UI confusion and break any future name-keyed lookup.
findings.recommendation: Disambiguate colliding names with spell-contextual prefixes or unique names (e.g. 'Lightning Chain Reaction' vs 'Rod Chain Reaction').

findings.description: handle_wall_of_fire_cancel (a casting-lifecycle function) lives in damage.rs alongside damage systems, mixing two concerns. All other casting-lifecycle code lives in casting.rs.
findings.recommendation: Move handle_wall_of_fire_cancel to casting.rs where the rest of the casting state-machine lives.

findings.description: RayPetrificationBeam and RayMindControlBeam are structurally identical (origin, direction, length, channel_progress, has_fired). Their Sweep/Glow companion component triples are also near-clones. The two beam systems driving them duplicate 80+ lines of channel/steer/fire logic.
findings.recommendation: Extract a generic ChanneledBeam { origin, direction, length, channel_progress, has_fired } component (or a typed enum variant) plus a shared channel_beam_logic helper, reducing each beam implementation to per-beam overrides (damage type, cone width, effect applied).

findings.description: MeleeRangeBonus(OGRE_MELEE_RANGE_BONUS) is inserted on the ogre at spawn but is never consumed. The shared melee.rs system excludes Boss entities (Without<Boss>), and ogre_combat computes its own range from raw hitbox.radius values. The constant OGRE_MELEE_RANGE_BONUS = 80.0 has no runtime effect.
findings.recommendation: Either remove MeleeRangeBonus from the ogre spawn bundle and delete OGRE_MELEE_RANGE_BONUS, or incorporate it into ogre_combat's range calculation.

findings.description: track_soul_power carries a copy-pasted doc comment ('Checks if it's time to spawn the Lich mid-game…') that belongs to check_lich_spawn in spawn.rs. The function actually tracks soul-power accumulation from undead kills. A spurious #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)] is also present on a 2-parameter function.
findings.recommendation: Replace the doc comment with an accurate description of soul-power accumulation; remove the #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)] annotation.

findings.description: resolve_finger_of_death inserts PendingUndeadRaise as a singleton Resource. The wizard's FoD spell (casting.rs line 653) also inserts this same resource when the finger_of_undeath talent is active. If both fire in the same frame, the second insert_resource call silently overwrites the first, losing one set of kill positions and preventing some corpse raises.
findings.recommendation: Switch PendingUndeadRaise to a Message (broadcast channel) so both sources enqueue independently, or accumulate positions into an existing resource instead of overwriting it.

findings.description: archer_ranged_combat declares `&mut AttackTiming` in its Query tuple but binds it as `_attack_timing` and never reads or writes it. This forces ECS to lock all AttackTiming components for exclusive write access every frame, blocking parallel systems (including archer_melee_combat) that also need AttackTiming.
findings.recommendation: Change `&mut AttackTiming` to `&AttackTiming` in the query, or remove it entirely since the ranged system uses ArcherMovementTimer for its cooldown.

findings.description: save_tutorial_progress loads the entire unified save file from disk, mutates one field, and writes it back on every tutorial completion or skip. Repeated quick-skips or completions incur redundant disk I/O round-trips.
findings.recommendation: Thread the mutation through the existing ResMut save-data resource so the on-disk file is written once per session boundary rather than on every tutorial event.

findings.description: try_start_tutorial accepts pending: Option<&PendingTutorials> but immediately discards it with let _ = pending; (line 53). The function then accesses PendingTutorials via a deferred world command. The parameter is misleading and forces callers to pass a borrow that is never read.
findings.recommendation: Remove the pending parameter from try_start_tutorial and update all six call sites. The world-command path already safely acquires PendingTutorials without a pre-borrowed reference.

findings.description: Efficiency calculation (1.0 - defenders_killed / total_defenders) is duplicated three times across saves.rs:38-45, saves.rs:235-241, and screen.rs:61-64, each with minor surface variation (one multiplies by 100, variable naming differs). This is the canonical game metric — any change must be made in three places.
findings.recommendation: Extract fn calculate_efficiency(kill_stats: &KillStats) -> f32 returning a [0,1] ratio to a single location in saves.rs or a new efficiency.rs, then call it from all three sites.

findings.description: The hotkey-button visual update loop (iterate all_hotkey_buttons, insert/remove ButtonActive + ButtonColors based on config.action_bar_slots) is copy-pasted identically between handle_hotkey_click (lines 211-231) and handle_number_key_assignment (lines 259-278).
findings.recommendation: Extract fn sync_hotkey_button_visuals(commands: &mut Commands, buttons: &Query<...>, config: &GameConfig, spell: Spell) and call it from both handlers.

findings.description: queue_notifications runs unconditionally in Update every frame across all app states including menus and the splash screen, where all 5 message readers are always empty. The two sibling systems in the same chain have run_if guards; this one does not.
findings.recommendation: Wrap the whole (queue_notifications, ...).chain() set with a run_if(is_gameplay_running) or run_if(is_local_wizard_active) condition consistent with the other guarded systems.

findings.description: Comment claims detect_rune_input 'consumes SpacebarPressed', but detect_rune_input reads ButtonInput<KeyCode> directly and never reads the SpacebarPressed message. This misleads anyone tracing the gamepad rune-activation flow and obscures a potential gap: for a gamepad-only RuneCaster, pressing South (A) fires SpacebarPressed but no system converts that to ActivateRuneSequence, so the rune sequence is never activated.
findings.recommendation: Correct the comment: detect_rune_input reads the physical keyboard binding and writes ActivateRuneSequence when the key is pressed. If gamepad-only rune activation needs to work, translate_runes should also emit ActivateRuneSequence when South is pressed (not rely on the keyboard path).

findings.description: init_toggle_resources calls crate::config::save_data::load_unified_save() — a synchronous filesystem read — inside a Bevy system on OnEnter(InGame). The unlocked wizard-type list is already reconstructable from in-memory resources rather than from disk.
findings.recommendation: Pass the already-in-memory GameConfig or a dedicated UnlockedWizardTypes resource populated at startup instead of re-reading the save file at game start. This avoids a blocking disk read in the OnEnter hot path.

findings.description: WizardType identity is compared against strings via format!("{:?}", wt) — the Debug representation is the canonical persistence key. If a variant is renamed, all existing save data silently loses that unlock. The ToggleModifier enum in the same file already demonstrates the correct pattern with a stable id() method.
findings.recommendation: Add a WizardType::to_save_id(&self) -> &'static str method (parallel to ToggleModifier::id()) and use it both when persisting and deserializing, removing the fragile Debug-format dependency.

findings.description: emit_water_ripples calls materials.add(StandardMaterial{...}) every WATER_RIPPLE_INTERVAL (1.2s), allocating a new GPU asset slot per ripple. With 3-4 ripples alive simultaneously this produces continuous new material registrations that are only cleaned up when the ripple entity despawns.
findings.recommendation: Pre-allocate a small pool of StandardMaterial handles in WaterRippleAssets (e.g. 8 slots) and recycle them, or use a custom thin material that encodes alpha as a uniform rather than per-entity StandardMaterial clones.

findings.description: sync_save_to_steam_cloud silently swallows std::fs::read failures with Err(_) => return. If the local save path exists but the file fails to open (permissions, lock, corruption), the Steam cloud is silently left stale with no log entry.
findings.recommendation: Replace `Err(_) => return` with `Err(e) => { warn!("Steam Cloud: failed to read local save for upload: {e}"); return; }`.

findings.description: update_timed_modifier::<TemporaryHitPoints>, update_timed_modifier::<SlowMovementModifier>, update_timed_modifier::<RootedModifier>, and update_timed_modifier::<HasteModifier> lack any_with_component guards, running every gameplay frame even when no unit has those components. Stunned (line 86) on the same block already has the guard.
findings.recommendation: Add .run_if(any_with_component::<T>) to each of the four unguarded update_timed_modifier calls, matching the pattern already used for Stunned, FrostAccumulation, FrozenSolidModifier, etc.

findings.description: definitions/mod.rs defines the TalentDefinition struct and the talent_definitions() dispatch function, making it a logic file rather than a pure mod/pub use re-exporter as required by project convention.
findings.recommendation: Move TalentDefinition struct and talent_definitions() into a sibling definitions/registry.rs, then mod.rs does only mod declarations and pub(crate) use re-exports.

findings.description: spawn_fire_smoke_puff and spawn_fire_particle_puff (lines 251-315) are near-identical private helpers. The only difference is one takes a material parameter and the other hardcodes assets.fire_particle.clone(). Duplication of ~28 lines of spawn bundle logic.
findings.recommendation: Merge into one function taking material: Handle<StandardMaterial>. spawn_fire_particle_puff becomes a one-liner calling spawn_fire_smoke_puff with assets.fire_particle.clone().

findings.description: hag_combat performs two O(n) scans over the full target set per hag per frame: first a has-target check (lines 418-435) to decide whether to reset the cooldown, then a nearest-target scan (lines 452-476) to pick the actual victim. The first pass is redundant and can be eliminated.
findings.recommendation: Collapse into a single pass: track nearest_target directly and only reset the cooldown and apply the attack if nearest_target is Some after the loop.

findings.description: apply_commander_auras allocates a new Vec (collect() at line 41) and a new HashMap<Entity, (Option<f32>, Option<f32>)> (line 45) every frame when commanders exist. With up to 9 commanders and hundreds of units, units_in_aura can hold hundreds of entries per frame. The system runs on every gameplay frame once commanders appear.
findings.recommendation: Pre-allocate both collections using Local<Vec<_>> and Local<HashMap<_, _>> system parameters, clearing them at the top of each invocation. This eliminates repeated heap allocation in the hot path.

findings.description: The doc comment for update_study_cursor says 'Reads the right stick' but the implementation at line 1469 calls read_left_stick_shaped. The companion study_cursor_edge_scroll also uses read_left_stick_shaped, confirming left stick is the intended cursor input — the comment is wrong and will mislead anyone reasoning about gamepad input routing.
findings.recommendation: Fix the doc comment to say 'Reads the left stick'. If right stick was intended for cursor movement (separate from pan), swap to a read_right_stick call and update both the comment and study_cursor_edge_scroll reasoning.

findings.description: pipeline.rs hosts update_crt_time, sync_colorblind_settings, sync_crt_enabled, sync_flicker_intensity, and sync_high_contrast — five main-world game systems not related to GPU pipeline initialization. This conflates render-world pipeline setup with main-world settings sync, making both harder to find.
findings.recommendation: Extract those five functions to systems.rs or a new sync.rs sibling. pipeline.rs should contain only render pipeline resources, init_*_pipeline functions, and ViewNode implementations.

findings.description: Plugin doc comment says 'the F3 toggle' but the system binds KeyCode::F4 (systems.rs:14). Wrong key documented in the only reference to the keybinding.
findings.recommendation: Change the doc comment to say 'F4 toggle' to match the actual binding in toggle_diagnostics.

findings.description: buff_defender_damage and buff_defender_resistance (lines 450-489) are structurally identical — fetch scalar, iterate team units, insert-component-if-positive-and-absent or remove-if-zero-and-present. The same pattern repeats a third time inside apply_guest_army_buffs (lines 872-890), meeting the 3-site shared-helper threshold.
findings.recommendation: Extract a generic helper function that handles the insert-or-remove-by-value logic for any buff component. The three call sites collapse to single lines, eliminating ~60 lines of duplication.

findings.description: receive_cauldron_buffs drains all of connection.incoming_messages into a Vec, handles only CauldronBuffsSync messages, then re-extends unhandled messages back. This is an ownership workaround for a shared message bus that causes two allocations per frame when unhandled messages exist and risks message ordering issues if multiple drain consumers run in the same frame.
findings.recommendation: Audit scheduling order of all incoming_messages.drain callers to confirm no consumer runs before receive_cauldron_buffs could consume messages it needed. Long-term, consider a typed channel or per-variant index rather than a drain-and-return pattern shared across 15+ systems.

findings.description: compute_save_signature uses toml::to_string(&save.player).unwrap_or_default() and the same for wizards. A serialization failure silently produces an empty string, so the written signature is wrong and every future load prints an integrity-mismatch warning with no root cause visible. Same pattern in progress.rs:144.
findings.recommendation: Use unwrap_or_else(|e| { warn!("Signature: failed to serialize player: {e}"); String::new() }) so the serialization error is surfaced in logs.

findings.description: utils.rs is 804 lines and mixes five distinct concerns: LocalSpellOrigin resource + lock-free atomic snapshot (~90 LOC), geometric math helpers (~120 LOC), heal helpers (PendingDefenderHeal + apply_spell_heal ~80 LOC), shared casting boilerplate (SpellCircleIndicator + build_wizard_input + cleanup helpers + cooldowns ~350 LOC), and ring-particle VFX shared between entangle/spike_growth (~100 LOC).
findings.recommendation: Split into spell_origin.rs, spell_math.rs, spell_heal.rs, casting_helpers.rs, ring_vfx.rs. Keep utils.rs as a re-export hub. The split is mechanical (no logic changes) but touches many downstream use imports across 30+ spell files.

findings.description: systems.rs is a single comment line with no exported symbols: //! Re-export hub for loading systems split into init.rs + queue.rs (Phase 18). It references an internal refactor phase tag (Phase 18) that is stale noise, and the mod systems declaration in mod.rs compiles a file that does nothing.
findings.recommendation: Remove systems.rs and its mod systems declaration from mod.rs. The Phase 18 refactor note can be placed in a git commit message or the CHANGELOG if historical context is needed.

findings.description: The ally snapshot build (Vec<(Entity, Vec3, Team, f32, f32, u32)>) and the find_heal_priority closure are written identically in three separate systems: update_healer_targeting (line 60), healer_start_heal_channel (line 325), and healer_tick_heal_channel (line 446). Any change to priority logic must be applied in all three places.
findings.recommendation: Extract a private `build_ally_snapshot` helper function (and optionally a named type alias for the tuple) so the mapping logic lives in one place.

findings.description: king_movement queries Option<&PolymorphedModifier> but binds it as `_polymorphed` and has no polymorphed-wander branch, unlike infantry, archer, and healer. If the polymorph spell can target the King (its targets query has no Without<King> filter), the King will silently ignore the effect.
findings.recommendation: Either add Without<King> to the polymorph spell's target query so Kings cannot be polymorphed, or add the wander branch in king_movement and remove the leading underscore.

findings.description: deserialize_action_bar calls HashMap::deserialize(deserializer).unwrap_or_default(), silently swallowing any deserialization error (e.g. renamed Spell variant in an old save) and returning all-None slots with no log output. The player's entire action bar is cleared without explanation.
findings.recommendation: Change to unwrap_or_else(|e| { bevy::log::warn!("Failed to deserialize action_bar_slots: {e}, resetting to empty"); HashMap::new() }).

findings.description: layout/setup.rs is 852 LOC and hosts system bodies (rebuild_panels_on_tab_change, compute_guest_pending, update_tab_active_state, update_mp_connected_indicator), resource/component definitions, and a SystemParam struct alongside the layout setup function — well above 300 LOC and mixing unrelated concerns.
findings.recommendation: Split into: layout/resources.rs (tab+view enums, marker components), layout/panel_rebuild.rs (rebuild_panels_on_tab_change, compute_guest_pending, MultiplayerPanelData), layout/tab_state.rs (update_tab_active_state, update_mp_connected_indicator), keeping setup.rs for setup_wizard_tower_layout + handle_tab_click + handle_back_button + escape_to_main_menu.

findings.description: animate_button_3d runs unconditionally every Update frame and iterates every ButtonAnimState entity. It has a per-entity early-exit when current ≈ target, but the query itself always runs. No system-level run_if gate exists.
findings.recommendation: Add a run_if condition (e.g. any_with_component::<ButtonAnimState>()) or track an 'any animation active' boolean resource to skip the system entirely when no buttons are animating.

findings.description: spawn_hud and spawn_mp_hud share ~130 lines of identical bottom-bar widget code: ammo display branch (lines 329-361 vs 561-591), mana-bar-with-reserved-fill branch (362-408 vs 592-638), and cast-bar-with-overlay section (410-457 vs 640-686). The 'Spells' button hide list (lines 217-221 and 497-501) is also duplicated. Every future widget change must be made twice.
findings.recommendation: Extract spawn_bottom_bars(parent, config) and spawn_hud_button_row(row, config) helpers and call them from both functions. Consider a widgets.rs sibling file to house them.

findings.description: handle_spike_growth_casting destructures talent_resources as (_talent_progress, ...) — BattleTalentProgress is injected as ResMut but immediately discarded. Talent progress tracking lives in apply_spike_growth_damage which injects it independently.
findings.recommendation: Remove Option<ResMut<BattleTalentProgress>> from the talent_resources tuple to avoid the unnecessary ResMut borrow in the casting system.

findings.description: apply_healing_plume_heal (line 280) and apply_cleansing_plume (line 387) are ongoing zone-effect runtime systems, not casting logic, yet they live in casting.rs (427 LOC total). The file declares itself 'casting and heal application' but owns zone-tick behavior, inflating it and blurring the casting/zone boundary.
findings.recommendation: Move apply_healing_plume_heal and apply_cleansing_plume to a new healing_plume/zone.rs. Update systems.rs re-exports and plugin.rs imports.

findings.description: HighlightState, update_highlight, and clear_highlight — approximately 100 lines of target-highlighting logic — live in casting.rs (486 LOC). Highlight management is a distinct visual concern unrelated to spell-casting state transitions.
findings.recommendation: Extract to mind_control/highlight.rs. handle_mind_control_casting takes highlight: Local<HighlightState> from the new module.

findings.description: Four call-sites across the module compare enum identity by formatting {":?"} debug strings against save-file string names (wizard_cards.rs:167, wizard_cards.rs:453, layout/setup.rs:28, multiplayer_tab/state.rs:186). A variant rename silently breaks the lookup without a compile error.
findings.recommendation: Add a fn save_key(&self) -> &'static str method to WizardType (and Spell) returning a stable on-disk string, then replace all format!("{:?}", …) identity comparisons with save_key().

findings.description: shards.rs is 868 lines — nearly 3× the 300-line threshold. It contains four independent concerns: projectile spawn+physics, explosion update+damage, talent effect systems (Sleet Storm, Absolute Zero, Blizzard, Ice Age, Frozen Ground), and snow VFX. Not a match/registry monolith.
findings.recommendation: Split into: projectiles.rs (spawn, physics, collision, spawn_ice_explosion), explosions.rs (update_ice_explosions), talents.rs (sleet_storm_evasion, absolute_zero, blizzard, frozen_ground), snow.rs (snow particles, storm ring).

findings.description: meteor.rs is 636 LOC and hosts four distinct concerns: projectile physics + smoke trail (lines 33–147), collision/impact with Aftershock and Volcanic Eruption sub-features (148–352), explosion animation + damage (396–505), and ground fire lifecycle—particles, damage, fade, cleanup (507–636). The project rule requires splitting files >300 LOC unless they are a single match-on-enum or asset registry.
findings.recommendation: Split into projectile.rs (movement, smoke trail, collision/impact), explosion.rs (animate + damage systems), and ground_fire.rs (particles, damage, fade, cleanup). Update systems.rs re-exports and mod.rs declarations.

findings.description: systems.rs is a glob re-export hub (pub use super::casting::*; pub use super::effects::*;) with a stale 'Phase 14' implementation note. Glob re-exports expose every public symbol from both files without callers knowing which file owns each.
findings.recommendation: Either drop systems.rs and have plugin.rs import directly from casting and effects, or replace glob re-exports with named re-exports for only the symbols plugin.rs uses. Remove the stale Phase 14 comment.

findings.description: Module-file comment `//! Re-export hub for wall_of_stone systems split (Phase 14).` is a stale internal refactoring phase number meaningless to future readers.
findings.recommendation: Change to `//! Re-exports all wall_of_stone systems from casting and lifecycle submodules.`

findings.description: update_weather_buttons hard-codes the keyboard prompt 'Clear Skies — Press Q/W/E' with no gamepad adaptation, while both peer archetype overlays (rune_display::adapt_rune_labels_to_input_device, roulette_display::adapt_prompt_to_input_device) swap text/font for the active controller style. A Meteorologist using a gamepad sees a keyboard prompt.
findings.recommendation: Add an adapt_weather_prompt_to_input_device system modeled on roulette_display's adapter that replaces 'Q/W/E' with appropriate D-pad glyphs when a gamepad is active, and register it in weather_bar/plugin.rs.

findings.description: components.rs is 444 LOC mixing ECS Resources, ECS Components, plain data structs (RunAggregateStats, LevelRunStats), utility functions (format_time, scorched_earth_mult, is_roguelite_mode, is_endless_mode), and module-wide constants. Project convention reserves the name components.rs for cross-cutting ECS types and says utility fns belong in feature files.
findings.recommendation: Split into: resources.rs (all #[derive(Resource)] types), modifiers.rs (ToggleModifier + ActiveToggles + RogueliteModifiers), run_stats.rs (LevelRunStats, RogueliteRunState, RunAggregateStats, format_time), and keep components.rs for the three actual #[derive(Component)] types (FortifiedHordeShield, WizardCycleFlash, ArchetypeUI).

findings.description: #[allow(dead_code)] on AppState and MenuState with the comment 'Variants will be used as game features are implemented' is stale — both enums are fully implemented. InGameState, MetaGameState, PauseMenuState, MultiplayerGameState, and SplashState carry no such attribute.
findings.recommendation: Remove the two stale #[allow(dead_code)] attributes from AppState (line 19) and MenuState (line 56).

findings.description: The AppState doc-comment state-transition table omits InGame → MainMenu (quit path) from the bulleted arc list, while it appears only in prose further down. InGameState::Tutorial has no transition documentation at all.
findings.recommendation: Add the missing arcs (InGame → MainMenu quit, Tutorial ↔ Running) to the AppState and InGameState doc-comment transition tables for completeness.

findings.description: The 'drain incoming_messages + match + collect unhandled + extend back' pattern is copy-pasted three times in this file (receive_swordcerer_spawn, apply_guest_avatar_input, receive_swordcerer_death) and also in meteorologist/networking.rs receive_weather_message. Four identical sites with no shared abstraction.
findings.recommendation: Extract a generic drain-and-dispatch helper (e.g., in a shared networking utility or inline within the file) so callers pass a closure and the requeue logic is written once.

findings.description: guest_systems.rs is a 4-line re-export hub (pub use super::guest_snapshot::*; pub use super::guest_visuals::*;). The star-re-exports widen visibility of every public symbol in those two files beyond what the convention requires, and the file provides no other value.
findings.recommendation: Remove guest_systems.rs and update plugin.rs to call guest_snapshot:: and guest_visuals:: directly. Update mod.rs to remove the guest_systems declaration.

findings.description: bolt.rs is 871 LOC and mixes five distinct concerns: gameplay impacts, null zone simulation, ghost visual tick, MP forwarding, plus six shared suppress/despawn helpers. Project convention caps non-cohesive files at 300 LOC.
findings.recommendation: Split into impacts.rs (update_dispel_impacts + update_null_zones), mp_dispel.rs (tick_ghost_dispel_impacts + forward_dispel_impacts_to_host + DispelForwarded), and suppress.rs (the six shared helpers). The glob re-export in systems.rs continues to work unchanged.

findings.description: apply_guardian_circle_buff and deal_aoe_force_damage use Vec3::distance() (3D Euclidean) for radius checks while every other spell in this batch uses xz_distance() (2D XZ plane). Inconsistent distance metric across the spell suite.
findings.recommendation: Replace transform.translation.distance(pos) with xz_distance(transform.translation, pos) in both functions for consistency.

findings.description: _clamped_cursor: Option<Vec3> is a dead parameter in guardian_circle_casting_logic — it is never read and prefixed with underscore, indicating it was planned but never implemented or was left over from a refactor.
findings.recommendation: Remove the dead parameter from guardian_circle_casting_logic and its call site.

findings.description: spawn_slider_row hard-codes the value display as format!("{}%", (current_value * 100.0) as u32). The roguelite tab uses sliders with range 0.2–3.0 (multipliers, not percentages), so displays '20%'–'300%'. The SliderRowConfig struct has no format field, so callers cannot override the display. The API is closed to extension for non-percentage sliders.
findings.recommendation: Add an optional value_format: Option<fn(f32) -> String> (or show_as_percent: bool) field to SliderRowConfig and use it in the Text::new(…) spawn to allow callers to supply their own display string.

findings.description: Item identity uses format!("{:?}", value) debug strings at 13+ call sites across setup.rs and rows.rs. This ties item key identity to Rust's Debug impl formatting — a rename of any Spell/Ingredient/UnitType/WizardType variant silently breaks save-file cross-reference without a compile error.
findings.recommendation: Add a stable .canonical_name() -> &'static str method on each enum that returns a fixed string. This makes the save-file contract explicit and renames become visible compile errors.

findings.description: BUTTON_REST_OUTLINE is used fully-qualified (crate::ui::constants::BUTTON_REST_OUTLINE) at lines 540 and 580, but BUTTON_3D_OFFSET_PRESSED, BUTTON_3D_OFFSET_REST, and BUTTON_PRESSED_OUTLINE are imported at lines 19-21. The import is incomplete, likely an oversight from when the import block was last edited.
findings.recommendation: Add BUTTON_REST_OUTLINE to the existing use crate::ui::constants::{...} import block at line 19 and remove the two full-path references.

findings.description: update_action_bar_slots runs every frame during InGameState::SpellBook and MultiplayerGameState::SpellBook (plugin.rs lines 110-114) without a resource_changed gate. The heavy icon/text update is guarded internally by if config.is_changed(), but the system still evaluates its full SystemParam list and the gun_state.is_changed() branch each frame the spellbook is open.
findings.recommendation: Add .run_if(resource_changed::<GameConfig>.or(resource_changed::<GunState>)) to the update_action_bar_slots scheduling, or split the gunslinger border highlight into a separate system already gated on resource_changed::<GunState>.

findings.description: compute_wave_staging and WaveStagingPlan::next_staging_point are deterministic seed-based functions with branching staging-point selection logic called every wave. No unit tests exist. The seed-based RNG makes output fully predictable for a given (seed, level, wave) tuple — ideal for table-driven tests.
findings.recommendation: Add tests: verify compute_wave_staging for both tunnels selects only from allowed ranges (LEFT_TUNNEL_STAGING, RIGHT_TUNNEL_STAGING); verify round-robin cycling in next_staging_point; verify remove_wave clears state.

findings.description: The combat system signature uses two levels of anonymous 16-tuple nesting with no named type aliases. Bevy's tuple-limit forces the nesting, but without aliases the destructuring is opaque and maintenance is error-prone across 95+ lines of parameter list.
findings.recommendation: Introduce type aliases (e.g. type AttackerSpellMods<'w> = (...)) for the inner tuple groups. No behaviour change, but makes the signature self-documenting and reduces edit surface when adding new modifier components.

findings.description: All system functions in host_systems.rs are declared pub even though none are referenced from outside src/game/multiplayer/. Only plugin.rs registers them. The convention elsewhere in the module uses pub(super).
findings.recommendation: Downgrade all host_systems system functions to pub(super) to match the module's visibility convention.

findings.description: systems.rs re-export hub carries the comment 'Phase 14'. All other re-export hubs in the project say 'Phase 16'. The stale phase number is meaningless development scaffolding.
findings.recommendation: Remove the phase annotation or replace it with a plain description: 'Re-export hub for squall systems.'

findings.description: Module-level comment reads '//! Re-export hub for ogre systems split (Phase 15).' The 'Phase 15' label is an internal planning artifact with no meaning to future readers.
findings.recommendation: Remove the phase reference: '//! Re-export hub — re-exports ogre systems from charge and combat submodules.'

findings.description: checks.rs is 1062 LOC and mixes many independent concerns: victory/defeat checks, encounter detection, boss defeat detection, roguelite modifier checks, completionist checks (Grand Council, Walking Library, Peak Wizard), and per-spell unlock detections. This is not a cohesive monolith exemption.
findings.recommendation: Split into concern-named sibling files: victory_checks.rs, defeat_checks.rs, encounter_checks.rs, boss_checks.rs, modifier_checks.rs, spell_unlock_checks.rs, completionist_checks.rs. The systems.rs wildcard re-export hub continues to unify them under the systems namespace for plugin.rs.

findings.description: convert_dead_to_corpses manually removes ~40 components in a single chained remove::<T>() block. Every new status-effect component must be added here by hand; omissions leave dead units with stale state.
findings.recommendation: Extract remove_all_status_effects(cmds: &mut EntityCommands) into units/status_effects.rs (or units/components.rs) so all death-cleanup paths share one authoritative list. Corpse conversion calls the helper once.

findings.description: 404 LOC mixing three distinct concerns: create-lobby flow (process_create_lobby_result, discard_stale_lobby), join-lobby flow (process_join_lobby_result, accept_incoming_join), and chat/presence updates (process_lobby_chat_updates, process_game_lobby_join_requested, process_game_rich_presence_join_requested, sync_coop_peer_name). Exceeds the 300-LOC rule without a single-concern exemption.
findings.recommendation: Split into create_lobby.rs (host-side create + discard_stale), join_lobby.rs (guest-side join + accept_incoming_join), and keep lobby_systems.rs for chat/presence drains.

findings.description: Inside apply_separation, current_positions is re-collected as a fresh Vec on each iteration of the COLLISION_ITERATIONS=4 loop. This is 4 heap allocations per frame over all units on the hot VelocitySystemSet path.
findings.recommendation: Collect current_positions once before the loop and update positions in-place each iteration, or reuse unit_data (already collected just above the loop) which already contains positions.

findings.description: systems.rs is a migration-artifact re-export hub labelled 'Phase 14' in its doc comment. It adds an indirection layer with no semantics and leaks internal history into the module surface.
findings.recommendation: Strip the 'Phase 14' comment. When F1/F2 splits are completed, remove the file entirely and have plugin.rs import from the split files directly or route through mod.rs.

findings.description: ignite.rs is 784 lines and contains four distinct concerns: (1) fire ignition logic (check_grease_ignition, update_grease_fire_spread), (2) burn/damage application (apply_grease_burn), (3) zone lifecycle (fade_grease_zone, cleanup_grease_zone, update_grease_regeneration, cleanup_grease_debuffs), and (4) zone spawning and VFX particles (spawn_grease_zone, spawn_grease_zone_vfx, spawn_grease_fire_smoke, update_grease_bubbles, update_grease_splatters). This violates the 300-line cohesion rule for non-match/non-registry files.
findings.recommendation: Split into: ignite.rs (fire ignition + fire spread), lifecycle.rs (fade, cleanup, regeneration, debuff cleanup), spawn.rs (spawn_grease_zone constructor), vfx.rs (fume/bubble/splatter/smoke VFX systems). Update the systems.rs re-export shim accordingly.

findings.description: combat.rs is 548 LOC covering six distinct concerns: spawning, facing override, targeting, melee combat, movement, and enrage. The module comment lists all six. Exceeds the 300-LOC hard limit.
findings.recommendation: Split into spawn.rs, facing.rs (or merge with targeting.rs), melee.rs, movement.rs, and enrage.rs.

findings.description: At 564 LOC, combat.rs exceeds the 300-line project limit and bundles four distinct concerns: soul-power accumulation and phase transition, movement (lich_movement + update_lich_targeting), combat targeting and FoD dispatch (lich_combat_targeting, lich_fire_beam, tick_lich_casting, resolve_finger_of_death), and visual/animation (update_lich_facing, update_lich_float, on_lich_cast_started, on_lich_cast_ended). This is not a single match-on-enum or asset registry exemption.
findings.recommendation: Split into soul_power.rs (track_soul_power + lich_phase_transition), movement.rs (lich_movement + update_lich_targeting), combat.rs (lich_combat_targeting + lich_fire_beam + tick_lich_casting + resolve_finger_of_death), and animation.rs (update_lich_facing + update_lich_float + on_lich_cast_started + on_lich_cast_ended). Update the systems.rs re-export hub accordingly.

findings.description: update_tutorial_content walks the Children tree two levels deep (lines 743-756) to update the Next button label, relying on the internal node structure of spawn_button remaining stable. Any layout refactor that adds or removes a wrapper node silently breaks the label update.
findings.recommendation: Tag the Next button's direct text child with a purpose-specific marker component (e.g. TutorialNextButtonLabel) at spawn time and query it directly, removing the tree-walk entirely.

findings.description: File is 393 lines mixing five unrelated concerns: device detection, virtual cursor integration, trigger-to-mouse translation, radial slot mapping, and settings sync + UI confirm/back. Exceeds the 300-line project ceiling and is not a single-concern monolith.
findings.recommendation: Split into device_detection.rs, virtual_cursor.rs, trigger_translation.rs, radial_slot.rs, with sync_gamepad_settings and emit_ui_confirm_back_messages folded into device_detection.rs or a new ui_systems.rs by affinity.

findings.description: tick_wizard_cycle contains a long match new_type block that directly calls into concrete archetype UI spawn functions (spawn_rune_display, spawn_roulette_display, spawn_arcanorouter_display, spawn_enter_fray_button) and initializes archetype-specific resources (GunState, FlamethrowerSfx). This makes game_mode an implicit dependency on every archetype's internal modules.
findings.recommendation: Add a spawn_archetype_ui method or dispatch via a WizardTypeChangedMessage that archetype plugins listen to, keeping game_mode decoupled from archetype internals.

findings.description: beams.rs (923 LOC) holds four unrelated beam attacks plus three shared helper functions. Still over-sized even before receiving the disintegration/petrification code from movement.rs.
findings.recommendation: After moving disintegration and petrification into beams.rs, split the file by attack: beams/disintegration.rs, beams/petrification.rs, beams/fear.rs, beams/mind_control.rs, beams/teleport.rs, beams/helpers.rs.

findings.description: charge.rs is 732 LOC covering three distinct concerns: the charge state machine (ogre_charge_system), charge visuals (update_ogre_charge_visuals), and the rock-throw system (ogre_rock_throw + ogre_throw_release), plus interleaved private helpers. Exceeds the 300-LOC hard limit with no cohesion exemption.
findings.recommendation: Split into charge.rs (state machine only), charge_visuals.rs (visual updates), rock_throw.rs (throw targeting + release), and move helpers like ogre_frame_uv_transform and facing_from_world_direction to a sibling animation.rs or utils.rs.

findings.description: handle_detail_slider_interaction (line 833) and handle_insight_bonus_slider_interaction (line 1020) are near-identical: same drag-start loop structure, same drag-clear loop, same dragging-entity extraction pattern, and near-identical fraction/clamp math. The comment at line 1020 acknowledges this ('Mirrors ... for spell sliders') without extracting shared logic. Any bug fix must be applied to both copies.
findings.recommendation: Extract shared helpers for drag-state detection and cursor-fraction-to-allocation computation, then thin both handlers to call them with spell vs. bonus parameters.

findings.description: Three near-identical settings_button_action functions exist across two files: interaction.rs:77 (main menu), interaction.rs:116 (pause menu), and src/ui/pause_menu/mp_settings.rs:92 (MP pause). All three share the same match arms for ResetTutorials, ClearProgress, and ResetControls and differ only in the Back arm's state transition target. This is 3-site duplication of non-trivial logic.
findings.recommendation: Extract a shared handle_common_settings_action(action, commands, bindings) helper that handles the three common arms and returns whether Back was pressed. Each context-specific function calls the helper then handles its own Back navigation.

findings.description: runtime.rs (499 LOC) merges three distinct responsibilities: continuous rebuild management (continuous_flow_field_rebuild, spawn_attacker/defender/assassin_field_rebuild helpers), obstacle event handling (handle_obstacle_events), and field sampling (sample_flow_fields, rally_to_spawn, sample_field_or_zero). The rebuild-vs-sampling split is conceptually clean and worth making explicit.
findings.recommendation: Split into rebuild.rs (rebuild orchestration, spawn_* helpers, handle_obstacle_events) and sampling.rs (sample_flow_fields, sample_field_or_zero, rally_to_spawn).

findings.description: systems.rs is a four-line glob re-export hub (pub use super::button_systems::*; pub use super::layout_helpers::*). This creates a second public path for every symbol in those two files, causing rustdoc duplication and making it unclear which file actually owns a given function. The 'Phase 16' comment suggests this was a migration shim that was never cleaned up.
findings.recommendation: Either delete systems.rs and migrate all callers to import directly from button_systems or layout_helpers, or document explicitly why the alias must be permanent. The dual-path situation should be resolved before it accumulates more callers.

findings.description: spawn_mark_indicators allocates a HashSet<Entity> every frame while ActiveMarkOfDeath entities exist by collecting all MarkVisualIndicator targets. This is an unconditional heap allocation on a per-frame hot path.
findings.recommendation: Replace the HashSet with a direct query check: query for MarkVisualIndicator on each marked entity directly (e.g., indicators_query.get(entity).is_ok()), eliminating the per-frame collection.

findings.description: spawn_deaths_ledger_explosion uses materials.get(&visual_assets.necrotic_pulse).cloned().unwrap_or_default() to clone the base material. If the handle is invalid, the explosion silently uses a default (black) material with no log output.
findings.recommendation: Add a warn!() when materials.get() returns None so the missing asset is observable.

findings.description: Indicator/SpellCaster management in handle_battle_hymn_casting is split across the outer match *casting_state block (lines 112-145) and battle_hymn_casting_logic (lines 239-277). The Channeling arm in the outer match calls cleanup_spell_caster but not casting_state.cancel(); that happens inside the inner function, making the 'cleanup and cancel always happen together' invariant non-obvious.
findings.recommendation: Fold the indicator/SpellCaster management into battle_hymn_casting_logic or use try_start_cast_with_indicator so the casting lifecycle is expressed in one place, matching the Haste pattern.

findings.description: systems.rs is a two-line wildcard re-export shim from setup.rs ('pub use super::setup::*'). Its comment labels it a 'Phase 18' migration artefact. After F1's setup.rs split this file will need to be re-evaluated to avoid becoming a misleading indirection layer.
findings.recommendation: After splitting setup.rs, enumerate specific symbols in systems.rs explicitly (no wildcard), or eliminate the file and expose them from mod.rs directly.

findings.description: load_and_apply_config manually copies every field from ConfigFile.game into GameConfig (30+ field assignments, lines 66–106), then immediately resets three of them to defaults (lines 112–114). Any future field added to GameConfig will be silently omitted from this constructor until someone remembers to add it here too.
findings.recommendation: Extract a GameConfig::from_config_file(config_file: &ConfigFile) -> Self constructor. Document which fields are reset post-construction and why (current_level, highest_level_achieved, efficiency_ratios are loaded later from the wizard save).

findings.description: setup, button_action, and relabel_continue_for_coop are declared pub (crate-public) but are only consumed by the sibling plugin.rs via use super::systems::{...}. No external module references them directly.
findings.recommendation: Change all three to pub(super) to enforce the module boundary.

findings.description: systems.rs is a glob re-export hub (pub use super::bolt::*; pub use super::casting::*) left from the Phase 14 split. This makes bolt and casting pub(crate) even though they are consumed only through this hub, and hides what is actually exported at the call site.
findings.recommendation: Either make bolt and casting plain mod (private) and keep the hub as the sole public interface, or remove systems.rs and have the plugin import from bolt and casting directly with explicit named imports.

findings.description: move_rolling_fog collects all attacker positions into a Vec<Vec3> every frame while RollingFogZone exists, even for a single zone.
findings.recommendation: Remove the Vec allocation by scanning units inline in the zone loop: maintain nearest_dist and nearest_dir over a single pass through units, no intermediate collection needed.

findings.description: cleanup_study_cursor_on_area_removed runs every Update frame with no run_if guard, polling RemovedComponents<SpellGraphArea> in all app states. The comment explains the reasoning (must fire outside WizardTower state to clear FocusNavInhibit), but the intent is undocumented as a deliberate exception to the project's run_if convention, which may cause future maintainers to add an incorrect guard.
findings.recommendation: Add an explicit comment marking this as a deliberate unconditional system. Optionally add a lightweight run_if(any_with_component::<SpellGraphArea>().or(condition_for_recently_active_tower)) to limit the polling window.

findings.description: cleanup_study_cursor_on_area_removed is registered in Update with no run_if guard (intentionally, to survive state transitions), but lacks an explanatory comment. Every other similarly-unconditional system in this file has inline rationale.
findings.recommendation: Add a one-line comment on the add_systems call explaining why the unconditional guard is intentional (e.g. 'Runs on any state so FocusNavInhibit is cleared even when leaving the tower entirely').

findings.description: Comment says 'random position within the pool' but the position is deterministically derived from time.elapsed_secs(). The sequence is not random — it is a deterministic pseudo-random walk that restarts identically each session.
findings.recommendation: Change comment to 'pseudo-random position derived from elapsed time' to avoid misleading future readers.

findings.description: receive_spell_visual_snapshot and receive_crdt_snapshot (host_systems.rs:987) both drain all incoming_unreliable into a temporary Vec, then split by type prefix and re-queue leftovers — two heap allocations per frame in the common path.
findings.recommendation: Use partition to split in one pass, or pre-allocate other_data with the known drain length as a capacity hint.

findings.description: nearest.as_ref().expect("checked").3 — the .expect() message "checked" is not self-explanatory as required by project convention. An unfamiliar reader cannot understand the invariant from the message.
findings.recommendation: Change to .expect("nearest is Some: loop guard ensures it was set before this point") or refactor to avoid the .expect() entirely with a conditional.

findings.description: clone_material_if_needed is a private per-entity material-cloning helper that duplicates the same deferred-clone pattern found in lightning_bolt.rs (lines 128-135). Two sites currently; extracting to spells/utils.rs would prevent a third copy.
findings.recommendation: Move clone_material_if_needed to src/game/units/wizard/spells/utils.rs as pub(crate) and import it from both lightning_bolt.rs and telekinesis/systems.rs.

findings.description: protocol.rs header and the NetworkMessage doc (line 70) both say 'WebRTC data channel'.
findings.recommendation: Change both occurrences to 'QUIC stream'.

findings.description: StatusEffectKind uses manual to_u8() / from_u8() methods while all other wire enums in the same file (SpellEffectKind, CastEventKind, SpellSoundId, AuraBubbleVariant, etc.) use TryFrom<u8>. Inconsistent pattern within the module.
findings.recommendation: Replace to_u8() / from_u8() with impl TryFrom<u8> for StatusEffectKind and Self as u8 inline, matching the rest of the file.

findings.description: compute_target_assist runs every frame during is_spell_effects_active and iterates all entities with Health (potentially 200+ units at high wave counts). When targeting assistance is disabled it exits early, but when enabled it is an unbounded O(N) scan regardless of whether any spell is being cast.
findings.recommendation: Add a run_if guard in plugin.rs such as wizard_is_casting_or_channeling.or(mouse_held_or_wizard_casting) so the O(N) scan is skipped when no local spell input is active.

findings.description: Doc comment at line 28 says 'Brutes spawn in the archer row alongside archers,' but the inline comment at line 36 says 'Brute spawns at the front with infantry.' The code calls attacker_spawn_position(0, 0.0) with no depth offset, matching infantry row placement, not the archer row. The two comments directly contradict each other.
findings.recommendation: Remove or correct the misleading doc comment at line 28 to match the code and inline comment. The spawn is at infantry row (no depth offset), not the archer row.

findings.description: Both dispeller/systems.rs and shielder/systems.rs use fully-qualified inline paths like crate::game::units::components::InMelee, ::Stunned, ::Petrified, ::CombatAnimation in the middle of query tuples and function bodies, while other symbols from the same module are already imported via a use statement at the top of the file.
findings.recommendation: Add InMelee, Stunned, Petrified, CombatAnimation to the existing use crate::game::units::components::{...} block in each file to eliminate the inline full paths.

findings.description: SCORE_BUTTON_STYLE and PAUSE_BUTTON_STYLE button constants are defined inline in systems.rs alongside lifecycle logic (init/cleanup, disconnect detection), mixing UI configuration with game state management.
findings.recommendation: Move them to the top of systems.rs grouped with the other score/pause constants, or extract to components.rs where the button action types live.

findings.description: TalentProgressBarFill.spell is marked #[allow(dead_code)]. The field is written at interaction.rs:338 but no system ever reads fill.spell — the component is used only as a marker. The allow suppresses a compiler signal that this field has no consumer.
findings.recommendation: Either drop the spell field and spawn TalentProgressBarFill as a plain zero-size marker, or remove #[allow(dead_code)] and write the consumer system that reads fill.spell for reactive bar updates.

findings.description: InsightAllocation (a runtime resource with domain methods: total_allocated, get, set, get_bonus, set_bonus) lives in components.rs alongside pure ECS marker structs. This mixes domain logic into what should be a pure type declaration file.
findings.recommendation: Move InsightAllocation and its impl block to study_tab/allocation.rs (or study_tab/resources.rs); it is exclusively owned by the study tab and is already pub(super) scoped.

findings.description: TalentProgressBarFill.spell is annotated #[allow(dead_code)], meaning the field is defined but never read. Suppressed dead-code is either unused cargo or an incomplete feature.
findings.recommendation: Remove the field if it is not needed, or connect it to the system that reads the progress bar fill color (removing the allow attribute once consumed).

findings.description: systems.rs is a pure 3-line re-export shim (pub(super) use super::setup::*). The indirection makes callers use systems::rebuild_on_state_change while code lives in setup.rs, obscuring provenance.
findings.recommendation: Either document the shim as a planned migration placeholder, or collapse it and have plugin.rs import from setup directly — or complete the split so systems.rs contains real system bodies.

findings.description: snapshot.rs header calls the unreliable channel a 'WebRTC data channel'. Line 481's SpellArcSnapshot.kind doc lists '6=Disintegrate' but kind 6 is no longer emitted — replaced by BeamSnapshot (confirmed by spell_sync.rs:598-602).
findings.recommendation: Fix header to say 'QUIC datagrams'. Remove '6=Disintegrate' from the kind doc list or annotate it as deprecated/unused.

findings.description: SpellSnapshotData doc says it 'Avoids exceeding Bevy's 16-parameter limit on a single system.' Bevy 0.18 does not have a 16-parameter system limit.
findings.recommendation: Update the comment to describe the actual reason (separating collection and transmission into two focused systems).

findings.description: The doc comment on handle_screen_flash_message reads 'Projects active black hole positions to viewport-local UV space for gravitational lensing…' — clearly copied from the lensing update function and never corrected. The actual function starts a screen-flash timer.
findings.recommendation: Replace with: 'Reads ScreenFlashMessage and starts the screen-flash animation, replacing any in-progress flash.'

findings.description: correct_ui_interaction_for_barrel allocates a Vec<(Entity, Vec2)> on the heap every PreUpdate frame when barrel distortion is active. The game has exactly one camera in practice, making this a gratuitous heap allocation per frame.
findings.recommendation: Use camera_query.iter().find_map(...) to get a single position directly, or use SmallVec<[_; 2]> to keep the allocation on the stack for the common single-camera case.

findings.description: correct_cursor_for_barrel_distortion runs every PreUpdate frame with no run_if guard, unlike every other Update system in this module which has explicit run_if guards per project convention. The function bails early when CRT is disabled, but the scheduler still dispatches and queries run unconditionally.
findings.recommendation: Add .run_if(any_with_component::<CrtEffectSettings>) to skip dispatch entirely before the camera entity is spawned (menu/loading states).

findings.description: detect_rune_input re-reads bindings.universal.activate and polls ButtonInput<KeyCode> directly — a second keyboard-polling site for the same physical key that detect_keyboard_input already polls for SpacebarPressed. Outputs differ (ActivateRuneSequence vs SpacebarPressed) but the duplicated polling pattern creates a hidden ordering dependency and splits activate-key semantics across two functions.
findings.recommendation: Document clearly in both functions that detect_keyboard_input owns the universal SpacebarPressed family while detect_rune_input exclusively owns ActivateRuneSequence. Long-term: have the rune system listen to SpacebarPressed and retire ActivateRuneSequence to unify the pathway.

findings.description: brute/systems.rs is 326 LOC and contains four distinct concerns: spawn_brute (~75 LOC), update_brute_targeting (~40 LOC), brute_movement (~90 LOC), and brute_rock_throw (~85 LOC). Project convention requires files exceeding ~300 LOC to be split unless they are a single-concern monolith.
findings.recommendation: Split into spawn.rs, targeting.rs, movement.rs, and rock_throw.rs. Plugin registration in plugin.rs is unchanged.

findings.description: The gameplay system block (lines 56-71) is a flat tuple without .chain(). Six systems all take &mut ArcaneCrystal — Bevy serializes them via conflict detection but execution order is non-deterministic. If two spell types hit the crystal in the same frame, crystal.remembered_spell is set by whichever system runs last.
findings.recommendation: Either add .chain() to make the order deterministic, or add a comment noting that last-writer-wins across spell types in the same frame is intentional behavior.

findings.description: The six-power distance attenuation formula (linear^6) is written out identically in play_sfx_scaled (line 197) and play_looping_sfx_at (line 418).
findings.recommendation: Extract into a private fn compute_attenuation(effect_pos: Vec3) -> f32 that calls audio_origin() internally, and have both sites call the helper.

findings.description: Three sites (lines 203, 328, 437) use format!("{}", x) where x is a char or Display type, when x.to_string() is the idiomatic spelling. Minor style inconsistency.
findings.recommendation: Replace format!("{}", rune.as_char()) with rune.as_char().to_string() and format!("{}", *sequence) with sequence.to_string().

findings.description: detect_window_resize, detect_window_move, detect_game_config_changes, detect_input_bindings_changes, mark_save_on_config_changed, and save_config_on_event all run every Update frame without run_if guards. Project convention (CLAUDE.md) requires run_if at the registration site. Systems rely on internal early-return guards instead.
findings.recommendation: Register change-detection systems with run_if: resource_changed::<GameConfig> for detect_game_config_changes, resource_changed::<InputBindings> for detect_input_bindings_changes, on_message::<ConfigChanged> for mark_save_on_config_changed, and on_message::<SaveConfigMessage> for save_config_on_event.

findings.description: The doc comment on contains_point_with_radius states 'The beam has uniform width along its entire length,' but the implementation at line 248 (distance <= self.beam_width() * cone_t + unit_radius) computes a cone that widens from zero at the origin to full width at the tip. The sibling method intersects_hitbox_cylinder correctly documents 'Cone radius widens linearly.'
findings.recommendation: Fix the doc comment on contains_point_with_radius to say 'cone that widens from 0 at the origin to full width at the tip.'

findings.description: SeedInputBox is declared pub(crate) but is only referenced within roguelite_tab.rs itself. No other file in the codebase imports or queries it.
findings.recommendation: Change to pub(super) to match the visibility of every other marker component in this file.

findings.description: LABEL_COLOR is a const that simply aliases TEXT_PRIMARY with no semantic distinction. It creates an indirection that implies differentiation where none exists and is used in 9 places.
findings.recommendation: Delete LABEL_COLOR and replace all 9 uses with TEXT_PRIMARY directly.

findings.description: Nine inline full-path references (crate::ui::constants::SLIDER_GAP, crate::ui::focus::Focusable, crate::ui::focus::ModalOverlay, etc.) appear inside spawner functions despite the file already importing from crate::ui::constants at the top. This is inconsistent with the file's established import style.
findings.recommendation: Add use crate::ui::focus::{Focusable, FocusableFlatBackground, ModalOverlay}; and use crate::ui::constants::{SLIDER_GAP, SLIDER_LABEL_FONT_SIZE, INSIGHT_COLOR}; to the top-level use block and remove the inline paths.

findings.description: seed_input_keyboard contains two structurally-identical loops for digit input: one for KeyCode::Digit0-9 and one for KeyCode::Numpad0-9. Both loops have identical bodies and the same length-guard check, producing ~20 lines of boilerplate.
findings.recommendation: Merge or chain the two arrays into a single iterator and replace both loops with one.

findings.description: update_run_summary despawns and re-spawns all RunSummaryContent children whenever RogueliteModifiers or PendingToggles is_changed(). The is_changed() guard (line 1491) is correct, but Bevy marks a resource changed whenever any ResMut borrow occurs, even without mutation. slider_button_action and slider_interaction both take ResMut<RogueliteModifiers>; any drag event triggers a summary rebuild even if the snapped value is unchanged.
findings.recommendation: Low risk given the roguelite_tab_active gate, but consider caching the last rendered summary lines and skipping the despawn/respawn if lines are identical.

findings.description: .expect("UI root exists") unwraps an iterator .next() inside a branch only reached when has_ui == true. Logically safe today, but a future refactor changing the early-return structure would introduce a silent panic.
findings.recommendation: Replace with explicit if let Some(root) = ui_root_query.iter().next() and an early return or warn! on None, making the invariant structural rather than runtime-asserted.

findings.description: PathfindingGrid::world_max carries #[allow(dead_code)] and is never read anywhere outside its constructor. It is stored in the resource but never consumed by any query or system.
findings.recommendation: Either remove the field and inline the grid_width/grid_height calculation directly in new(), or demote visibility to non-pub since no external code reads it.

findings.description: smooth_with_lic clones self.directions (a Vec<Vec3> of 480k elements, ~5.76 MB) on every field rebuild so it can read originals while writing smoothed values. Rebuilds happen on background threads so the main thread is not blocked, but each rebuild allocates and then drops ~5.76 MB of heap.
findings.recommendation: Store a reusable scratch buffer on FlowField (or pass one in) and copy into it instead of cloning, eliminating the per-rebuild heap allocation.

findings.description: The module-level doc-comment says 'Receives the latest unit state snapshot from the host and creates/updates/despawns ghost entities' — this describes apply_state_snapshot, which was moved to guest_snapshot.rs in the Phase 18 split. The file now owns pick_material, spawn_spell_effect, and handle_game_over_message.
findings.recommendation: Update the module-level doc-comment to accurately describe what the file now contains.

findings.description: update_fire_particle_time iterates all FireParticleMaterial assets every frame (under is_spell_effects_active) even when no fire particles are alive. update_aura_sphere_time does the same for AuraSphereMaterial. Constant per-frame cost regardless of whether relevant entities exist.
findings.recommendation: Guard update_fire_particle_time with any_exist::<FireOrangeSmokePuff>() and update_aura_sphere_time with any_exist::<AuraBubbleVfx>(), matching the pattern used for all other systems in the plugin.

findings.description: CAULDRON_COOP_POSITION is byte-for-byte identical to CAULDRON_POSITION (both compute WIZARD_POSITION + CAULDRON_OFFSET with the same signs and fields). The duplicate creates a maintenance hazard: if the SP cauldron position changes, the co-op constant silently diverges.
findings.recommendation: Replace with pub const CAULDRON_COOP_POSITION: Vec3 = CAULDRON_POSITION; to make the aliasing explicit and automatically correct when the base constant changes.

findings.description: WaveSpawnedMessage (and its wave_number field, suppressed with #[allow(dead_code)]) is written by tick_wave_timer but has zero MessageReader subscribers anywhere in the codebase. The message is registered and sent but never consumed.
findings.recommendation: Either add a subscriber (e.g., a UI wave-number notification) or remove the message type and the MessageWriter injection from tick_wave_timer.

findings.description: BlackHole.damage_type field is annotated #[allow(dead_code)] and never read. All damage call sites in gravity.rs hard-code DamageType::Force directly.
findings.recommendation: Remove the field, the allow annotation, and the DAMAGE_TYPE constant from constants.rs (or keep it as a doc-comment-only reference).

findings.description: aerialist_combat takes Res<ArcherAssets> and calls crate::game::units::archer::systems::spawn_arrow() directly. The aerialist module has a hard runtime dependency on archer's internal resources and spawn function. If arrow VFX is ever decoupled from the archer module, aerialists break silently.
findings.recommendation: Extract spawn_arrow and its asset references into a shared units/projectiles.rs helper, or add the arrow mesh/material to AerialistAssets so the aerialist module is self-contained.

findings.description: Health is initialized as Health::new(crate::game::constants::UNIT_HEALTH * 1.2) with a magic multiplier inline. All other units in scope and across the codebase define an explicit named constant (TELEPORTER_HEALTH, DISPELLER_HEALTH, SHIELDER_HEALTH). The 1.2 has no documentation.
findings.recommendation: Add pub const AERIALIST_HEALTH: f32 = crate::game::constants::UNIT_HEALTH * 1.2; to aerialist/constants.rs and use it in spawn.

findings.description: Two spellings for the same boolean: spawn_hud creates `let is_gunslinger = config.wizard_type == WizardType::Warglock` and uses it locally; spawn_mp_hud (line 560) inlines the same comparison directly. The variable name 'is_gunslinger' also mismatches the public archetype name 'Warglock'.
findings.recommendation: After extracting the shared widget helper (F03), a single predicate survives. Align the name with the WizardType variant (is_warglock) or add a WizardType::is_gunslinger() predicate method.

findings.description: The spawn-time 'hide Spells button' check (lines 219-221, and 498-501) lists Warglock | Randomancer | RuneCaster explicitly, while the runtime guard in hud_button_action (line 705) uses config.wizard_type.uses_exclusive_casting() which only covers RuneCaster | Randomancer (not Warglock). A future archetype added to uses_exclusive_casting() would get the runtime guard but not the spawn-time button hide.
findings.recommendation: Either extend uses_exclusive_casting to cover Warglock, or add a separate fn hides_spell_button() predicate that both the spawn-time check and hud_button_action call.

findings.description: The ammo display is initially populated using GunType::MachineGun.max_ammo() / GunType::MachineGun.ammo_per_ui_piece() (= 12 pieces) in both spawn_hud and spawn_mp_hud (lines 348-350 and 578-580). This hardcodes the initial piece count to MachineGun without verifying it is the largest across all gun types.
findings.recommendation: Replace with GunType::all().iter().map(|g| g.max_ammo() / g.ammo_per_ui_piece()).max().unwrap_or(12) or extract a GUN_MAX_UI_PIECES constant derived from all variants.

findings.description: apply_spell_damage_to_rocks defines a local closure `let xz_distance = |a, b| …` instead of using the shared xz_distance from crate::game::units::wizard::spells::utils, which terrain/utils.rs already imports.
findings.recommendation: Add `use crate::game::units::wizard::spells::utils::xz_distance;` at the top of boulder/systems.rs and remove the local closure.

findings.description: NetworkedSpellEffect and SpellEffectKind are referenced with fully-qualified crate::… paths three times in the file (lines 51-55, 137-140, 507-510) instead of using top-level imports. Inconsistent with the rest of the codebase.
findings.recommendation: Add use crate::game::multiplayer::components::NetworkedSpellEffect and use crate::networking::snapshot::SpellEffectKind at the top of boulder/systems.rs.

findings.description: refresh_spell_visuals_for_wizard (defined in units/wizard/spells/visual_assets.rs) is registered in three different plugins with no comment at the game_mode site explaining why this plugin owns the config.is_changed() trigger for it.
findings.recommendation: Add an inline comment explaining that this registration recolors Excremage materials when tick_wizard_cycle changes config.wizard_type mid-game, to distinguish it from the other two registrations.

findings.description: process_music_fade re-reads game_config.effective_music_volume() on every tick. If the user scrubs the volume slider mid-crossfade, the fade target changes silently, potentially producing a jarring volume jump during an active transition.
findings.recommendation: Add a target_volume: f32 field to MusicFade and snapshot the target at spawn time so the fade arc is stable regardless of concurrent GameConfig changes.

findings.description: track_for_state is a private helper function with no explicit visibility modifier. Project conventions use pub(super) for all module-internal helpers to make intent explicit.
findings.recommendation: Add pub(super) to track_for_state to match the visibility style used for all other helpers in the module.

findings.description: When GameConfig is absent during the resource_added::<MusicAssets> trigger (early startup race), check_music_transition silently returns without spawning any music. There is no log warning, so this silent skip is invisible in logs.
findings.recommendation: Add warn!("check_music_transition: GameConfig not yet available, skipping") before the early return so the skip is observable during debugging.
