findings.description: `WallOfStoneTalentParams` derives only `Clone` — no `Debug`. `WallTalents` wrapping it therefore also lacks `Debug`, making it opaque in inspector tools and log macros.
findings.recommendation: Add `#[derive(Debug)]` to `WallOfStoneTalentParams` and `WallTalents`.

findings.description: #[allow(dead_code)] on FireballExplosion.damage_type is a false negative: the field is read at projectile.rs:550 (TerrainDamageMessage) and projectile.rs:577 (apply_spell_damage_with_team). Also affects Fireball.damage_type (line 15) which is genuinely unread, and WallOfFireEffect.damage_type (wall_of_fire/components.rs:22) which is bypassed by a hardcoded DamageType::Fire in the damage system.
findings.recommendation: Remove #[allow(dead_code)] from FireballExplosion.damage_type (field is live). For Fireball.damage_type and WallOfFireEffect.damage_type, either thread the field through consistently or remove it and its constructor parameter.

findings.description: _wizard: &Wizard parameter in lightning_rod_casting_logic is never read (prefixed underscore to suppress warning). It is passed from the outer handler as dead weight. Similarly, _wizard_entity: Entity in chain_lightning_casting_logic (chain_lightning/casting.rs:226) is never used inside the function.
findings.recommendation: Remove _wizard from lightning_rod_casting_logic and its call site (casting.rs:215). Remove _wizard_entity from chain_lightning_casting_logic and its call site.

findings.description: HEALER_SPRITE_TINT (Color::srgb(0.75, 0.65, 0.65)) is byte-for-byte identical to archer/constants.rs ATTACKER_SPRITE_TINT. Silent value duplication means tuning one will not follow through to the other.
findings.recommendation: Either confirm the identical value is intentional and add an explanatory comment, or re-export the archer constant from healer/constants.rs.

findings.description: load_my_unlocked_content() calls Spell::all().to_vec() unconditionally on every invocation, allocating a Vec of all spells. This function is called in sync_lobby_with_connection, process_lobby_messages, and commit_host_start.
findings.recommendation: Return Spell::all() as a &'static [Spell] slice (the caller can convert), or cache the unlocked spell list in the lobby resource once at PlayerInfo receive time rather than recomputing on every call.

findings.description: Same stale 'Blocks spell input...' doc comment copy-pasted onto update_wave_display. Describes a completely different system.
findings.recommendation: Replace with a correct doc comment describing update_wave_display.

findings.description: Tooltip top-offset is BUFF_BOX_SIZE + BUFF_BOX_GAP + 20.0 + 10.0. The 20.0 and 10.0 addends are unexplained magic numbers with no comment or constant name.
findings.recommendation: Replace with named constants or add an inline comment explaining what the addends represent (e.g., HUD margin offset + label height).

findings.description: Three static step arrays (WIZARD_TOWER_STEPS, TIME_TRAVEL_STEPS, STUDY_STEPS) belong to deprecated TutorialId variants. They are reachable only through TutorialId::steps() but no live trigger fires those IDs. StartBattleButton and TimeTravelButton HighlightTarget variants referenced in these arrays are never tagged.
findings.recommendation: Replace the step arrays for deprecated IDs with &[] empty slices to make the dead content obvious and remove ~88 lines of unreachable tutorial text.

findings.description: ParsedManualContent is a Resource defined inside systems.rs. Project convention places Resources and Components in components.rs (or a dedicated resources.rs), not in system files.
findings.recommendation: Move ParsedManualContent to manual/components.rs or a new manual/resources.rs alongside the other manual types.

findings.description: The rebuild: bool field of ObstacleChanged is decorated #[allow(dead_code)] and its doc-comment states it 'is no longer needed'. It is set at ~30 call-sites across the codebase (always false or true with no effect) but is never read. This is dead state every call-site must populate.
findings.recommendation: Remove the field and all rebuild: ... struct literal entries from the ~30 call-sites across terrain, spells, and multiplayer files.

findings.description: #[allow(dead_code)] on Spell::category() is stale. The method is actively called from src/ui/cauldron_menu/setup.rs:426, src/ui/compendium/rows.rs:361,370, and src/ui/wizard_tower/layout/decorations.rs:45. The annotation suppresses a warning that no longer fires and may mask a future real dead-code regression.
findings.recommendation: Remove the #[allow(dead_code)] attribute from Spell::category().

findings.description: update_spell_range_indicator uses .iter().next() on a With<LocalWizard> query (single-entity) and on the SpellRangeCircle query (also single). Every other wizard system uses .single()/.single_mut(). The .iter().next() pattern silently succeeds when an entity is missing, potentially hiding a logic bug.
findings.recommendation: Replace both .iter().next() guards with .single()/.single_mut() to be consistent with the rest of the codebase and get a clear diagnostic on unexpected missing-entity conditions.

findings.description: pulse_spell_range_indicator runs every frame and calls materials.get_mut() on the range circle material, dirtying it unconditionally. This triggers a GPU material re-upload every frame even when the alpha change from the previous frame is imperceptibly small.
findings.recommendation: Apply the material change only when the computed alpha differs from the current material alpha by more than a small epsilon (e.g., 0.005), using set_if_neq or a manual comparison before calling get_mut.

findings.description: The in-code comment for tier-3 talent option 2 reads '// Unstable Resonance', but the player-visible talent name in talents/definitions/frost.rs:62 is 'Beam Fireballs'. The field TalentConfig::resonance and internal constants section header in constants.rs also use the 'resonance' label.
findings.recommendation: Rename internally to beam_fireballs / beam_fireballs: bool (field, comment, constant section header) to align with the player-visible name and avoid confusion.

findings.description: The 'pseudo-random angle' for annihilation resonance fireballs uses beam.resonance_timer * 137.5. After resonance_timer -= MINI_FIREBALL_INTERVAL (1.5s), the timer resets to ~0..delta_secs (~0..0.016s), making angle ≈ 0..2.2 radians. Fireballs always cluster in roughly the same direction instead of spreading around the full circle as the comment 'Random outward XZ direction' implies.
findings.recommendation: Replace beam.resonance_timer with time.elapsed_secs() as the angle seed (matching the approach in emit_impact_particles line 407), or draw from the seeded-RNG resource for deterministic full-circle spread.

findings.description: update_null_zones uses is_gameplay_running while every other system in the plugin uses is_spell_effects_active. The asymmetry is intentional (null zone is host-only simulation) but has no comment, making it look like a bug to future maintainers.
findings.recommendation: Add a brief inline comment: '// host-only: NullZone is gameplay simulation, not a guest-side visual' to make the deliberate asymmetry self-documenting.

findings.description: TWIN_STARS_MANA_MULT = 1.0 is a no-op multiplier. Multiplying by 1.0 changes nothing; the const name misleads readers into thinking it adjusts cast cost for Twin Stars.
findings.recommendation: Either tune it to a real value or remove the constant and inline a comment explaining Twin Stars cost is intentionally unchanged.

findings.description: find_nearest_enemy uses manual (dx*dx + dz*dz).sqrt() for the spell-range check (line 399) but xz_distance for the target-proximity check (line 402). Both measure 2-D ground-plane distance; the inconsistency is confusing and the sqrt form is slower.
findings.recommendation: Replace the manual sqrt form at line 399 with xz_distance(transform.translation, wizard_pos) <= spell_range.

findings.description: update_graph_edge_positions (line 1247) and update_insight_edge_positions (line 1341) are structurally identical — same graph_area lookup, same clip_line_to_rect call, same angle/midpoint rotation computation. They differ only in the query filter (SpellGraphEdge vs. InsightConstellationEdge).
findings.recommendation: Extract a position_edge_segments free function parameterized over the edge component, or merge into a single system with an Or<> query filter on a shared HasEndpoints interface.

findings.description: SELECT_BUTTON_STYLE and EXPAND_BUTTON_STYLE are defined using fully-qualified paths (crate::ui::components::ButtonStyle, crate::ui::constants::BUTTON_BG, etc.) instead of use imports. Every other file in this module uses imports.
findings.recommendation: Add use crate::ui::components::ButtonStyle and use crate::ui::constants::{BUTTON_BG, BUTTON_BORDER, TEXT_PRIMARY, TEXT_MUTED} imports and remove the inline path qualifications from the const definitions.

findings.description: PHILOSOPHERS_STONE_CONFIG has effect: BrewEffect::BuffDurationMultiplier(1.0), which is a no-op (is_noop() returns true). The stone's actual function — removing dilution — is implemented in Recipe::dilution_factor(), not through BrewEffect. This creates a misleading contract when callers iterate recipe effects.
findings.recommendation: Add a dedicated BrewEffect::RemovesDilution variant so the stone's effect is visible when iterating effects(), or at minimum add a doc-comment to the config explaining the sentinel no-op.

findings.description: ignite_trees_from_fire (and ignite_bushes_from_fire in bush/systems.rs:80-87) use raw fully-qualified crate::… paths inline in Query type parameters rather than top-level use imports. This is inconsistent with all other files in the module and makes function signatures unreadable.
findings.recommendation: Add use imports for FireballExplosion, MeteorExplosion, DisintegrateBeam, WallOfFireEffect, and MeteorGroundFire at the top of both files to replace the inline paths.

findings.description: Four timer types (ChannelChangeTimer, ScreenFlashTimer, VignettePulseTimer, DesaturationTimer) each implement an identical fn intensity() -> f32 sine-bell curve, fn is_finished() -> bool, and a new() constructor. This is four copies of the same ~10-line pattern with trivial parametric differences.
findings.recommendation: Define a private SineTimer { elapsed: f32, duration: f32 } struct with tick(), t(), and is_finished() helpers. Have each timer delegate to it. Future timing-curve changes become a one-line edit.

findings.description: init_locked_ingredients calls load_unified_save() (a synchronous disk read) on the main thread inside OnEnter(AppState::Loading). The loading queue already performs a save-data pass elsewhere, making this a redundant disk read every run.
findings.recommendation: Fold the locked-ingredient cache population into the existing save-load pass during loading to eliminate the redundant disk read.

findings.description: MultiplayerSession.host_spells and guest_spells are both #[allow(dead_code)]. They are populated at session creation but never read during gameplay. The only active consumer of guest spells is coop.rs which carries its own intermediate struct.
findings.recommendation: Remove both fields from MultiplayerSession to eliminate dead state.

findings.description: Four methods (fire_interval, is_hold_to_fire on GunType; two helpers in resources.rs) are tagged #[allow(dead_code)], indicating they are defined but never called. Suppressing the warning rather than removing the code leaves dead weight.
findings.recommendation: Audit whether these methods are actually called anywhere. If not, remove them. If they are intentional public API for UI consumers, replace the allow with a doc comment explaining the intended caller.

findings.description: Doc-comment on spawn_ice_projectiles reads 'Applies or inserts a SlowMovementModifier on an entity.' — copied verbatim from the apply_or_insert_slow helper directly above it.
findings.recommendation: Fix doc-comment: 'Spawns ice projectiles into the storm area on a timed interval.'

findings.description: let seed = time_secs * 7.1 + i as f32 * 1.618_034 is named 'seed' but does not seed the RNG — the rng.random_range() calls above it are independent. 'seed' is only used to compute a phase offset for animation variation, creating a misleading impression.
findings.recommendation: Rename to phase_seed and add a comment: '// deterministic phase offset — does not seed the RNG'.

findings.description: decay_absolute_zero_slow performs an O(units × storms) double-loop. With Absolute Zero there is at most one storm so this is benign in practice, but the inner loop still re-iterates the storms query for every unit when a storm exists.
findings.recommendation: Pre-collect the single active AZ storm's position and radius into an Option<(Vec3, f32)> before the unit loop, eliminating repeated query iteration.

findings.description: XZ-plane distance is computed four different ways in the same file: manual (dx*dx+dz*dz).sqrt() at lines 235 and 269, the xz_distance() utility at line 471, and Vec3::new(x,0,z).length() at line 573. All are semantically identical but inconsistent, increasing cognitive overhead and risk of divergence in future edits.
findings.recommendation: Standardize to xz_distance(a, b) from crate::game::units::wizard::spells::utils, which is already used in the same file.

findings.description: GreaseOilSlickDebuff::new() and GreaseRegenerating::new() (line 173) are zero-argument constructors. Rust convention for zero-arg constructors whose body is Self { field: constant } or Self { field: 0.0 } is #[derive(Default)]. Other components in the codebase use Default.
findings.recommendation: Replace fn new() -> Self on both structs with #[derive(Default)]. Update call sites from ::new() to ::default() or direct struct literal.

findings.description: spawn_cluster_bombs contains magic numbers 100.0 (min distance), 300.0 (max distance), 0.4 (flight_time), and 15.0 (visual_radius base) with no named constants. These are tuning values absent from constants.rs.
findings.recommendation: Extract CLUSTER_BOMB_MIN_DISTANCE, CLUSTER_BOMB_MAX_DISTANCE, CLUSTER_BOMB_FLIGHT_TIME, and CLUSTER_BOMB_VISUAL_RADIUS into fireball/constants.rs.

findings.description: move_fireballs carries the doc comment 'Local wizard fireball casting — reads mouse input.' This is copied from casting.rs; move_fireballs does not read mouse input at all.
findings.recommendation: Replace with 'Advances all fireball projectiles by their velocity each frame.'

findings.description: find_target_near_position_excluding constructs Vec3::new(pos.x, 0.0, pos.z) manually four times to compute XZ-plane distances (lines 387, 406, 410-413) instead of calling the xz_distance helper from spells/utils.rs, which is used elsewhere in the same codebase and in chain.rs.
findings.recommendation: Replace the four manual Vec3::new(pos.x, 0.0, pos.z).distance(...) expressions with xz_distance from spells/utils.rs.

findings.description: #[allow(dead_code)] on ChainLightningBolt.damage_type is stale. The field is actively read: bolt.damage_type is copied into ChainLightningBoltSnapshot and then used in every apply_spell_damage_with_team call in chain.rs. The annotation misleads future readers into thinking the field is vestigial.
findings.recommendation: Remove the #[allow(dead_code)] attribute from ChainLightningBolt.damage_type.

findings.description: plugin.rs defines three non-registration functions: has_telekinesis_talent (a run-condition factory, lines 51-61), init_transmutation_stacks (lines 63-65), and cleanup_transmutation_stacks (lines 67-69). The project convention is plugin.rs = Bevy registration only.
findings.recommendation: Move has_telekinesis_talent and the two lifecycle fns into systems.rs or a new resources.rs alongside TransmutationStacks. plugin.rs should contain only app.add_systems / app.add_plugins / run_if wiring.

findings.description: CauldronState::Cooldown { remaining } is marked #[allow(dead_code)] and is never constructed anywhere in the codebase. The tick() branch for Cooldown is unreachable in practice. This is scaffolding left over from a planned feature that was never implemented.
findings.recommendation: Remove the Cooldown variant and its tick() branch, or add a // TODO: comment explicitly documenting the planned design intent to prevent future confusion.

findings.description: CauldronState::active_recipe() is annotated #[allow(dead_code)] and is genuinely unused. CauldronState::progress() is also annotated #[allow(dead_code)] but IS called externally from src/ui/in_game/bars.rs:129 — its annotation should be removed.
findings.recommendation: Remove #[allow(dead_code)] from progress(). Delete active_recipe() if it has no planned callers.

findings.description: Doc comment on init_talent_resources says 'InGameState::Running can be re-entered (e.g., after spell book or pause menu)' but this note will be stale if the system body is moved per finding T1.
findings.recommendation: Update or move the comment alongside the function body when addressing T1.

findings.description: In the Quick Foundations loop, `result.obstacle_bounds` is overwritten each iteration — only the last wall's bounds are sent via `WallPlaced`. The first wall's pathfinding removal bounds are silently dropped on the remote peer.
findings.recommendation: Send one `WallPlaced` message per wall segment, or document that the full snapshot already covers both walls and the `WallPlaced` removal path is the only affected case.

findings.description: `WallOfStoneCaster` is lazily inserted on the wizard entity on the first frame the spell is cast, causing a one-frame early-return that silently drops the input for the very first cast attempt.
findings.recommendation: Insert `WallOfStoneCaster` in the wizard spawn bundle or in an `OnEnter(AppState::InGame)` system, removing the lazy-insert fallback path entirely.

findings.description: teleporter_ranged_combat inserts CombatAnimation::new_casting() when firing a bolt attack. Every other ranged unit (dispeller_ranged_combat:633, archers) uses new_attack(). The teleporter has no attacking_texture in TeleporterAssets so it silently reuses casting_texture with semantically wrong animation state.
findings.recommendation: Either add an attacking_texture to TeleporterAssets and use new_attack(), or document explicitly in code why the cast animation is intentionally used for bolt attacks.

findings.description: update_channel_state defines a push_sorted closure inline inside a match arm and calls it three times for infantry, brute, and commander candidates. Each call block has an identical .filter().map().collect() pattern differing only in the query variable name.
findings.recommendation: Extract push_sorted as a module-level fn and collapse the three identical candidate-gather blocks into a shared collect_ally_candidates(iter, pos) -> Vec<(Entity, f32, f32)> helper.

findings.description: The 'set both SP and MP state to Running' pattern is copy-pasted three times inside button_action for StartBrew, CancelBrew, and Close actions (lines 57–83). Six near-identical lines repeated three times.
findings.recommendation: Extract a local closure or inline helper close_cauldron_menu(sp, mp) to de-duplicate the three identical state-transition blocks.

findings.description: update_detail_panel_on_selection_change is already gated by .run_if(resource_changed::<IngredientSelection>) in plugin.rs:47. The manual if !selection.is_changed() { return; } guard at line 99 is therefore dead code — selection.is_changed() is always true when the system body executes.
findings.recommendation: Remove the redundant early-return guard at interaction.rs:99.

findings.description: Both UpgradeToElite (lines 513-526) and UpgradeToCommander (lines 550-566) contain identical boilerplate to copy transform and hitbox through a ParamSet before calling the upgrade helper. The shared helper upgrade_systems::get_transform_and_hitbox exists for exactly this purpose and is used in wave_systems.rs but not here.
findings.recommendation: Call upgrade_systems::get_transform_and_hitbox in both arms, passing the ParamSet projections. This removes the duplicated pattern and keeps the shared helper consistently used.

findings.description: The doc-comment on process_spawn_queue still reads Initializes the loading progress tracker and spawn queue — copied verbatim from the old monolith before init.rs was split out. The function no longer initializes anything; it drains the queue.
findings.recommendation: Replace the doc-comment with one that describes the actual responsibility: processing the SpawnQueue in per-frame batches, breaking at command-flush boundaries, and transitioning to InGame when complete.

findings.description: Two separate steps are both labeled // 13. in init.rs (lines 375 and 378). The broader step numbering sequence also skips 7, 9, 10 and jumps from 6 to 8 then to 11 before reaching 13. The numbers no longer correspond to any meaningful ordering count.
findings.recommendation: Renumber the step comments to match the actual enqueue order, or drop the numbers entirely and keep only the descriptive text. Numbering drifts every time a step is inserted.

findings.description: Lines 198-199 contain inner use crate::game::constants::{BOSS_CYCLE_LENGTH, get_tier} and use crate::game::constants::{is_boss_level, is_lich_level} statements inside the function body. All four symbols are already in scope from the module-level glob use crate::game::constants::* at line 7. The redundant re-imports imply those symbols are not covered by the glob, misleading readers.
findings.recommendation: Remove the two inner use statements inside init_loading_progress.

findings.description: SCORCHED_EARTH_DURATION_MULT at line 436 carries the doc comment 'Last level of a roguelite run (tier 4 boss, level 25).' which is the doc for ROGUELITE_MAX_LEVEL (line 441), not the duration multiplier. Copy-paste error from an adjacent constant.
findings.recommendation: Fix the doc on SCORCHED_EARTH_DURATION_MULT to read 'Duration multiplier applied by the Scorched Earth toggle.'

findings.description: Six methods in ActiveToggles and ToggleModifier carry #[allow(dead_code)] attributes. In a binary crate the compiler already warns only for truly unreachable items. If these methods are reachable from UI or save-data code the attribute is misleading; if genuinely unused the methods should be removed.
findings.recommendation: Audit each #[allow(dead_code)] site. Remove the attribute, run cargo check, and delete any methods that are confirmed unreachable.

findings.description: NetworkConnection.ping_timer is a public f32 field that is never written to or read outside of reset(). The iroh transport has no application-level ping tick implementation.
findings.recommendation: Remove ping_timer from NetworkConnection. Ping latency arrives via TransportEvent::PingUpdate from the Steam transport only.

findings.description: WizardAnimation has a new() method returning all-zero fields but does not #[derive(Default)]. This is inconsistent with Bevy idiomatic usage and triggers the Clippy new_without_default lint. CastingState on the same file correctly derives Default.
findings.recommendation: Add #[derive(Default)] to WizardAnimation (both fields zero-initialize naturally) and replace WizardAnimation::new() call sites with WizardAnimation::default(), or keep new() and add an explicit impl Default for WizardAnimation.

findings.description: BASE_SPELL_RANGE (3000.0) is declared as an inline const inside apply_bonuses_to_wizard_stats rather than in constants.rs. This is the same base spell range used by the wizard system; if it diverges silently the Arcanorouter's range calculations will be wrong.
findings.recommendation: Move BASE_SPELL_RANGE to arcanorouter/constants.rs or game/units/wizard/constants.rs so it shares a single source of truth with the wizard setup code.

findings.description: set_selection and has_talent on ActiveTalents are both marked #[allow(dead_code)] and are never called anywhere in the codebase outside the struct definition.
findings.recommendation: Remove both methods if unused, or remove the dead_code suppression and let the compiler enforce usage. Suppressed dead public API is misleading.

findings.description: #[allow(dead_code)] appears on BindingContext (line 120), BindingAction (line 132), the InputBindings impl block (line 362), and is_bindable_key (line 668). All of these are actively imported and used by src/ui/main_menu/settings/ and src/game/achievements/checks.rs. The annotations are stale and will suppress legitimate warnings if a variant is removed.
findings.recommendation: Remove all four #[allow(dead_code)] attributes in input_bindings.rs. Run cargo check to confirm nothing is genuinely unused.

findings.description: Petrified is referenced via full inline crate path (crate::game::units::components::Petrified) at lines 81 and 287, while all other units::components types are imported cleanly at the top of the file.
findings.recommendation: Add Petrified to the existing 'use crate::game::units::components::{...}' import block at line 9.

findings.description: Doc comment 'Computes talent parameters from the player's active talent selections.' is attached to spawn_plague_cloud.
findings.recommendation: Replace with: 'Spawns a plague wind cloud entity and registers it as a pathfinding obstacle.'

findings.description: Function doc says 'With Revenant Lord talent, only one corpse is raised (no channeling phase)' but the code unconditionally calls casting_state.start_channeling() at end of the Casting branch — channeling still begins with Revenant Lord active.
findings.recommendation: Update doc: 'With Revenant Lord, the first corpse is raised at cast completion; the RevenantLord component then drives passive auto-raise via tick_revenant_raise. Channeling proceeds normally.'

findings.description: EYE_SHEET_WIDTH and EYE_SHEET_HEIGHT are exported pub(in crate::game) but are never imported outside utils.rs. Only EYE_FRAME_UV (computed from them) is consumed by callers. The two raw dimension constants leak internal derivation detail unnecessarily.
findings.recommendation: Demote to private module-level constants since they are only used to define EYE_FRAME_UV in the same file. Remove the pub(in crate::game) visibility.

findings.description: is_on_screen is a general camera-NDC utility in the shared boss helpers but has exactly one call-site (dark_mage/ai.rs:547). Zero reuse outside dark_mage adds unnecessary shared-surface area.
findings.recommendation: Inline into dark_mage/ai.rs where it is the sole consumer, or add a doc comment explicitly noting it is intended for future reuse to justify keeping it here.

findings.description: The doc comment above justina_chain_lightning reads 'Builds a WalkingAnimation configured for the hag sprite sheet (4x4 frames)' — a copy-paste artifact from hag_walking_animation in core.rs. The function casts chain lightning and has nothing to do with walking animations.
findings.recommendation: Replace with a correct description of the chain lightning ability system.

findings.description: update_ray_eye_movement allocates a Vec<(Entity, Vec2)> every frame for the 5-eye separation pass. Only 5 entries, but it is a needless heap allocation in a hot update system.
findings.recommendation: Replace with a [Option<(Entity, Vec2)>; 5] stack array populated in-place before the main eye loop.

findings.description: Three inline Color::hsla(25.0, …) literals for the contact, medium, and ambient shadow layers in spawn_page_container's BoxShadow block are not named constants. They differ from the exported SHADOW_COLOR constant in lightness/alpha. Future palette changes will miss these three literals.
findings.recommendation: Extract as FRAME_SHADOW_CONTACT, FRAME_SHADOW_MEDIUM, and FRAME_SHADOW_AMBIENT constants in constants.rs and replace the literals.

findings.description: spawn_dot_leader uses an inline TextColor(Color::hsla(0.0, 0.0, 0.3, 1.0)) with no named constant. This specific shade is lighter than TEXT_PLACEHOLDER and darker than any named muted color, so future palette sweeps will miss it.
findings.recommendation: Extract as DOT_LEADER_COLOR in constants.rs.

findings.description: The slider track background uses an inline BackgroundColor(Color::srgb(0.2, 0.2, 0.2)) with no named constant, inconsistent with all other slider styling coming from named constants.
findings.recommendation: Extract as SLIDER_TRACK_BG in constants.rs alongside the other SLIDER_* constants.

findings.description: Stale development comment: '// NOTE: The rest of this function was the old placeholder. The spawn_controls_subsection and spawn_key_binding_row helpers are defined below.' This refers to a completed refactor and provides no value to readers.
findings.recommendation: Remove the stale comment.

findings.description: Inline Color::srgb(0.3, 0.8, 0.3) (victory green), Color::srgb(0.8, 0.3, 0.3) (defeat red), and Color::srgb(0.3, 0.6, 0.9) (accent blue) are repeated 7 times in setup.rs without named constants.
findings.recommendation: Add VICTORY_COLOR, DEFEAT_COLOR, ACCENT_COLOR to constants.rs.

findings.description: items_container.single() failure is silently skipped with let Ok(container) = ... — if two ItemsContainer entities exist due to a despawn bug, item list rebuilds are silently suppressed with no log.
findings.recommendation: Add a warn! in the else path, or use .expect() since single ItemsContainer is a programming invariant.

findings.description: WaveStagingPlan::has_wave iterates all HashMap keys with .keys().any(|(w,_)| *w==wave) instead of two O(1) contains_key probes. remove_wave uses retain (also O(n)). With at most ~20 entries this is harmless but inconsistent with direct-lookup idioms used elsewhere.
findings.recommendation: Replace has_wave with self.wave_points.contains_key(&(wave, SpawnTunnel::Left)) || self.wave_points.contains_key(&(wave, SpawnTunnel::Right)) for O(1) lookup.

findings.description: DISORIENTING_VAPORS_CHANCE is referenced via a deep inline super::super:: path inside the function body rather than a top-level use import, while all other fog_cloud types are imported at the file top.
findings.recommendation: Add a top-level use import for DISORIENTING_VAPORS_CHANCE consistent with how other constants from the same module are referenced.

findings.description: ASSASSIN_ATTACK_SPEED_BONUS and shielder/assassin damage constants are accessed via full inline crate:: paths scattered through the function body rather than top-level use imports, while component types are imported at the top.
findings.recommendation: Move all per-unit constants used in the function body to top-level use imports for visual consistency and easier discoverability.

findings.description: derive_seed uses hand-rolled LCG-style mixing with wrapping_mul and fixed magic constants. Passing purpose=0 collapses the entire output to 0 regardless of master/level. No assertion or documentation guards against this degenerate case.
findings.recommendation: Add a debug_assert!(purpose != 0) at the start of derive_seed, or document the invariant that SEED_PURPOSE_* constants must be non-zero. Alternatively, replace the ad-hoc mixing with a standard hash function to avoid degenerate inputs.

findings.description: update_beam_eclipse falls back to a magic number 500.0 for spell_range when no Wizard entity is found (wizard_query.iter().next().map(|w| w.spell_range).unwrap_or(500.0)). This value is not derived from any constant or configuration.
findings.recommendation: Extract to constants::DEFAULT_SPELL_RANGE_FALLBACK with a doc comment, or gate the system on any_with_component::<Wizard>() to avoid the fallback entirely.

findings.description: teleport_casting_logic accepts _primed_spell: &PrimedSpell (underscore prefix indicating unused) as its 5th parameter. The outer system passes primed_spell but the inner function never reads it.
findings.recommendation: Remove the dead parameter from teleport_casting_logic. The empowerment value is accessed in the outer wrapper directly.

findings.description: Timer-complete branch spawns spawn_aura_bubble_synced (non-contracting) for the source position, while the early-release branch (line 548) spawns spawn_aura_bubble_contracting_synced. Visual effect differs depending on whether the player releases early or waits — appears unintentional.
findings.recommendation: If intentional, add a comment explaining the design; otherwise make both paths use spawn_aura_bubble_contracting_synced for the source to match the 'circle shrinks away' metaphor.

findings.description: Doc comment `/// Computes talent parameters from active talent selections.` is a copy-paste from casting.rs:29 and precedes `handle_wall_of_stone_cancel` — completely wrong function description.
findings.recommendation: Replace with `/// Cancels an in-progress Wall of Stone drag on right-click.`

findings.description: `animate_sinking_walls` queries all `WallOfStone` entities and filters `if wall.sinking` in the loop body, iterating all standing walls every frame for zero effect. No `SinkingWall` marker component parallels the existing `WallRising` pattern.
findings.recommendation: Add a `SinkingWall` marker component inserted when `sinking` becomes true, and narrow the query to `With<SinkingWall>`, consistent with the `WallRising` pattern.

findings.description: Both casting.rs and damage.rs have dual imports: `use super::constants;` and `use super::constants::*;`. The bare `constants` import is redundant when the glob is also present. Other spell modules (fireball, magic_missile) use only one form.
findings.recommendation: Remove the `use super::constants;` line and use only `use super::constants::*;`, or qualify constants individually without the glob.

findings.description: Material cloning for vine rings uses materials.get(&assets.entangle_vine).cloned().unwrap_or_default(). If the asset handle is invalid, unwrap_or_default() silently falls back to a default white material with no log output, making asset load failures invisible.
findings.recommendation: Use if let Some(base_mat) = materials.get(&assets.entangle_vine).cloned() { ... } else { warn!("entangle vine material not loaded"); } to surface load failures via bevy::log.

findings.description: DARK_MAGE_DAMAGE_MULTIPLIER = -0.3 and DARK_MAGE_MELEE_DAMAGE_REDUCTION = 0.4 are both active simultaneously with no comment explaining their interaction. The lich uses only DamageMultiplier(-0.5), not both. It is unclear if the two stack or if one is redundant.
findings.recommendation: Add an explicit comment documenting both are intentional and what each affects, or verify in the damage pipeline that they do not stack unintentionally and remove the redundant one.

findings.description: Both the resources and systems sub-modules are declared pub(in crate::game), but no consumer outside src/game/units/boss/lich/ imports from lich::resources or lich::systems. LichAssets is used only internally; the systems module is a re-export hub consumed only via plugin.rs (which uses super::systems::*).
findings.recommendation: Tighten both declarations to pub(super) to match their actual visibility scope and prevent accidental coupling.

findings.description: LichFingerOfDeath::new() hard-codes the initial cooldown as the literal 1.0 with only an inline comment. All other timing values in this module are named constants in constants.rs.
findings.recommendation: Add const LICH_FOD_INITIAL_COOLDOWN: f32 = 1.0; to constants.rs and reference it from ::new() for consistency with the rest of the tuning surface.

findings.description: ELITE_ATTACK_SPEED_BONUS has the doc comment 'Elite attack speed bonus as percentage (FUTURE - not implemented in MVP).' This is incorrect: the bonus is applied in combat_systems/melee.rs:256 and the component is inserted in loading/upgrade_systems.rs:85 and multiplayer/spawning.rs:550. The same stale note appears in elite/components.rs:38.
findings.recommendation: Remove the 'FUTURE - not implemented in MVP' language from both elite/constants.rs and elite/components.rs and replace with accurate descriptions.

findings.description: TeamFilter::Both is marked #[allow(dead_code)] and has zero call sites anywhere in the codebase. It has been suppressed since the commander module was introduced with no documented future plan.
findings.recommendation: Either remove TeamFilter::Both entirely, or add an explicit comment like '// Reserved for future cross-team buffing (e.g., necromancer aura)' to make the intent clear and justify the suppressor.

findings.description: Doc comment 'Blocks spell input when the mouse is interacting with a UI button...' is copy-pasted from block_spell_input_on_button_interaction onto update_mana_bar. The comment describes a completely different system.
findings.recommendation: Replace with a correct one-liner describing update_mana_bar's purpose (updating the mana bar fill width from the local wizard's Mana component).

findings.description: HagIdentity is mapped to array index 0/1/2 via a three-way match block repeated three separate times in update_boss_health_bar (lines 659-664, 670-674, 683-687). RayEyeType (same file, line 579) exposes an index() method that eliminates this repetition for ray eyes. HagIdentity has no such method.
findings.recommendation: Add pub const fn index(self) -> usize to HagIdentity in game/units/boss/hags/components.rs and replace all three match blocks with identity.index().

findings.description: respawn_menu_on_toggle polls two ECS queries every Update frame while in CauldronMenu state to check whether the menu entity is absent. Under normal play the menu is always present, so both queries run and find results on every frame. The condition (menu absent) is true for only one frame after rebuild_menu_on_brew_state_change despawns it.
findings.recommendation: Drive the respawn from a message or a Local<bool> dirty flag set by rebuild_menu_on_brew_state_change, rather than polling every frame.

findings.description: BACK_BUTTON_STYLE is referenced as crate::ui::main_menu::BACK_BUTTON_STYLE. The canonical constant lives at crate::ui::constants::BACK_BUTTON_STYLE. Other UI modules (manual, wizard_tower) import from ui::constants directly, creating an inconsistency.
findings.recommendation: Import from crate::ui::constants::BACK_BUTTON_STYLE instead of the main_menu re-export path.

findings.description: The doc comment on setup_game_over_screen says 'Saves efficiency for current level to config' and 'This system runs BEFORE setup_game_over_screen'. Both are false: the function does not save efficiency (that is save_efficiency_to_config in saves.rs), and the sentence refers to itself as a different system. The comment was copied from a sibling system.
findings.recommendation: Replace with accurate doc: setup_game_over_screen spawns the score-screen UI entities given the current game outcome and kill stats.

findings.description: Seed display (small grey text, font_size 14.0, Color::srgba(0.6, 0.6, 0.6, 0.8)) is spawned with identical node parameters and styling in both game_over/screen.rs:413-420 and pause_menu/main/systems.rs:322-330.
findings.recommendation: Extract fn spawn_seed_label(parent: &mut ChildSpawnerCommands, seed: u64) into ui/systems.rs and call it from both sites.

findings.description: Stale section header 'Soiled Surprise' at line 677 is displaced: check_master_brewer with its own section header immediately follows, then check_soiled_surprise appears at line 709. The Soiled Surprise header is orphaned from its function.
findings.recommendation: Reorder so check_soiled_surprise immediately follows its section header (swap with the Master Brewer block), or merge both into a single contiguous block.

findings.description: Some BattleEndedMessage handlers call grant_achievement_insight after do_unlock (check_first_victory, check_the_king_is_dead, check_chain_reaction, etc.) while others (check_immortalized, check_the_grind_never_stops, check_one_more_level) do not. No comments explain whether the omissions are intentional or oversights.
findings.recommendation: Add a brief inline comment next to each do_unlock call either calling grant_achievement_insight or explicitly noting '// no insight bonus for this achievement' to make the asymmetry auditable.

findings.description: check_master_brewer compares ingredients via format!("{:?}", i) to match save-file serialization. This creates an implicit contract: renaming any Ingredient variant changes its Debug repr, silently breaking the completionist check for existing players without a compile-time warning.
findings.recommendation: Add a '// IMPORTANT: must match save_data.rs ingredient serialization' comment. Long-term, introduce an Ingredient::save_key() -> &'static str method returning a stable identity string, used by both save_data.rs and checks.rs.

findings.description: detect_out_of_range iterates all non-wizard, non-corpse entities every gameplay frame and filters by Team::Defenders inside the loop body. Attackers and Undead are fetched from ECS storage and immediately discarded.
findings.recommendation: Add a Defender marker component or change the query filter to only include entities with Team component set to Defenders, avoiding unnecessary iteration of all non-wizard units.

findings.description: Pond::obstacle_bounds and Tree::obstacle_bounds (tree/components.rs:65) are annotated #[allow(dead_code)]. No callers exist anywhere in the codebase. Dead methods with suppressed warnings are a maintenance trap.
findings.recommendation: Remove both methods if nothing calls them. If they are intended as public geometry helpers for future use, make them pub and remove the #[allow(dead_code)].

findings.description: tick_pond_shocked allocates a heap Vec to collect and sort targets on each arc pulse (every 0.8s). Given POND_SHOCK_MAX_TARGETS = 4, this is a small but unnecessary heap allocation in a gameplay system.
findings.recommendation: Replace Vec with SmallVec<[(Entity, Vec3, f32); 8]> and use select_nth_unstable instead of full sort, or leave as-is given the 0.8s interval. Either way document the choice.

findings.description: trample_flora allocates Vec<u32> every gameplay frame when flora entities exist (up to 80 items). The post-loop config.saved_flora.retain uses Vec::contains which is O(n) on trampled_ids.
findings.recommendation: Despawn and collect trampled flora IDs into a SmallVec or use a per-entity break+despawn pattern directly in the inner loop, removing the post-loop retain and the per-frame allocation.

findings.description: suppress_staging_targeting runs on every frame for every staging attacker with no early-exit when the query is empty. Unlike check_wave_activation (which correctly guards with if staging_query.is_empty() { return; }), this system does not short-circuit when there are no staging attackers.
findings.recommendation: Add if query.is_empty() { return; } at the top of suppress_staging_targeting to match the pattern used by check_wave_activation and avoid unnecessary iteration after all waves have activated.

findings.description: CLOSE_CALL_DISTANCE is imported from swordcerer::constants inside the function body. This constant triggers a generic kill-proximity achievement and has no swordcerer-specific logic; the dependency on a wizard-archetype module is misleading.
findings.recommendation: Move CLOSE_CALL_DISTANCE to an achievements constants file or the achievements module, removing post_combat's dependency on a wizard-archetype module for a generic trigger.

findings.description: Death-asset resources are split into death_assets and death_assets_2 with no explanation of the split boundary. The naming is opaque and the reason (Bevy 16-tuple limit) is not documented.
findings.recommendation: Rename to basic_death_assets / specialist_death_assets (or similar semantic names) and add a brief comment explaining the 16-element tuple limit that forces the split.

findings.description: stats.total_time as i32 is cast without a bound guard when submitting to the clear-time leaderboard. The base-score path at line 130 applies .min(9_999.0) for the penalty term but no corresponding cap exists for the time submission.
findings.recommendation: Cap with .min(i32::MAX as f32) as i32 or add a doc comment explaining the implicit upper bound.

findings.description: spawn_status_effects_section is a UI spawning function (builds Bevy UI nodes via ChildSpawnerCommands) living inside the game layer at game/units/wizard/. Its only two callers are src/ui/compendium/rows.rs and src/ui/spell_book/setup.rs. UI code belongs in src/ui/ per the project's feature-sliced architecture.
findings.recommendation: Move spawn_status_effects_section and effective_status_effects to a shared UI helper module (e.g., src/ui/spell_book/status_effects.rs or a new src/ui/spell_info/) and update the two UI callers to import from there.

findings.description: PsychopathPlugin registers apply_defender_spell_vulnerability only on OnEnter(AppState::InGame), not OnEnter(AppState::MultiplayerGame). If Psychopath is ever re-enabled for multiplayer the vulnerability application will silently not fire.
findings.recommendation: Either add an OnEnter(AppState::MultiplayerGame) hook with run_if(is_psychopath), or add an explicit comment in the plugin stating that Psychopath is intentionally disabled in multiplayer so the missing hook is documented.

findings.description: The doc comment on process_pending_undead_raises reads '/// Computes talent-modified parameters for Finger of Death.' — a copy-paste from the compute_fod_params function in casting.rs.
findings.recommendation: Replace with a correct doc comment describing what process_pending_undead_raises does: finding corpses near kill positions and resurrecting them as undead infantry.

findings.description: update_reapers_scythe allocates a full FingerOfDeathBeam struct every frame tick (once per active sweep) solely to call beam.contains_point and beam.beam_width(). FingerOfDeathBeam::with_talents clones the 12-field FodTalentParams on every allocation.
findings.recommendation: Inline the contains_point hit-test and beam_width formula directly using local variables from ReapersScytheSweep fields; remove the per-frame struct allocation.

findings.description: The nearest-corpse search uses best.as_ref().map(|(_, d)| *d).unwrap_or(f32::MAX) — a verbose pattern. More critically, if a primary beam and a chain beam both fire on the same frame, commands.insert_resource(PendingUndeadRaise { ... }) at casting.rs:653 silently overwrites any prior raise list from the same frame, potentially dropping kill positions.
findings.recommendation: Use best.map_or(f32::MAX, |(_, d)| d) for readability. For the overwrite issue, consider accumulating positions into an existing resource or using a message/event to avoid same-frame data loss.

findings.description: The doc comment on line 33 reads '/// Helper to write an obstacle event for a grease zone.' — this is the description of write_grease_obstacle from casting.rs, copy-pasted and left attached to check_grease_ignition. check_grease_ignition has no correct doc comment.
findings.recommendation: Replace line 33 with an accurate description of check_grease_ignition, e.g. '/// Scans all active fire sources and ignites any overlapping non-ignited, non-regenerating grease zones.'

findings.description: fade_grease_zone calls materials.get_mut(material_handle) unconditionally every frame for every active grease zone. Bevy's Assets::get_mut marks the asset as changed regardless of whether values actually change, triggering a GPU re-upload every frame. During the non-fading window (remaining >= FADE_DURATION, fade == 1.0) the base_color write is a no-op in terms of visible effect but still marks the material dirty.
findings.recommendation: Guard the base_color write behind `if fade < 1.0 { ... }`. The iridescent sheen genuinely animates every frame so its write is acceptable, but the redundant alpha write during the fully-opaque window should be skipped.

findings.description: The four-line doc comment 'Computes the axis-aligned bounding box of a rotated wall...' describes wall_obstacle_bounds from casting.rs, but it is directly attached to handle_wall_of_fire_cancel. This is copy-paste residue from a file reorganisation.
findings.recommendation: Replace the stale doc comment with one that correctly describes handle_wall_of_fire_cancel.

findings.description: WALL_SMOKE_INTERVAL is a private constant defined inline in damage.rs while all other WallOfFire timing constants live in constants.rs. Splits the single source of truth for tuning values.
findings.recommendation: Move WALL_SMOKE_INTERVAL to constants.rs as pub(super).

findings.description: Doc comment 'Computes talent parameters from active talent selections.' is attached to tick_plague_bearer_aura — clearly copied from casting.rs when the file was split.
findings.recommendation: Replace with: 'Ticks the Plague Bearer aura: spawns smoke VFX and applies periodic poison damage to nearby living units.'

findings.description: tick_plague_bearer_aura and handle_undead_detonation use apply_damage_to_unit which bypasses SpellShield and spell_vulnerability, while all other spell damage in scope uses apply_spell_damage_with_team. The king's SpellShield does not block plague aura or detonation damage.
findings.recommendation: Document this explicitly as 'plague is indiscriminate, bypasses shields by design' in the function headers, OR switch to apply_spell_damage_with_team if the design intent is consistency with other spells.

findings.description: handle_undead_detonation injects Res<Time> and immediately assigns let _t = time.elapsed_secs() which is never used. Dead code leftover from an earlier VFX pass.
findings.recommendation: Remove the time: Res<Time> parameter and the let _t assignment.

findings.description: Doc comment on update_traitors_mark_aura reads '/// Computes talent parameters from active talent selections.' — a copy-paste from the adjacent compute_talent_params function. The function does not compute talent params; it applies/removes the Demoralized debuff.
findings.recommendation: Replace with a correct summary, e.g. '/// Applies/removes the Demoralized debuff on enemies near a Traitor's-Mark unit.'

findings.description: RayEyeState::new() is a manual constructor equivalent to Default::default() but the type does not derive Default. This is inconsistent with Bevy component conventions and makes initialization less ergonomic.
findings.recommendation: Implement Default for RayEyeState with active: [true; COUNT] and remove the redundant new() method, or keep new() and also derive/impl Default.

findings.description: The use crate::game::units::boss::utils::indicator_rotation; import appears at line 811 — the very last line of the file — after all function bodies. Rust permits this but it violates the universal project convention of grouping all use statements at the top.
findings.recommendation: Move the import to the top-of-file use block alongside the other imports.

findings.description: The circle indicator spawning code for DarkMeteor (lines 476-487) and PlagueCloud (lines 515-527) are near-identical 12-line duplicates differing only in the radius scale constant.
findings.recommendation: Extract a spawn_circle_indicator(commands, assets, fill_material, center, radius) -> Entity helper and call it for both DarkMeteor and PlagueCloud arms.

findings.description: DarkMageSpellQueue::new() and DarkMageEnrage::new() are zero-argument constructors whose bodies are trivially Self { field: default_value }. The idiomatic pattern for zero-arg constructors is #[derive(Default)].
findings.recommendation: Replace the no-arg new() impls with #[derive(Default)] on DarkMageSpellQueue and DarkMageEnrage.

findings.description: PlagueHazardBroadcast (a marker Component) is defined at the bottom of spells.rs rather than in components.rs where all other Dark Mage components live.
findings.recommendation: Move PlagueHazardBroadcast to components.rs.

findings.description: find_spell_target allocates a Vec<Vec3> via .collect() every call, then performs O(n²) cluster scoring over it. This is called each frame the mage is Idle with a spell queued.
findings.recommendation: Eliminate the intermediate allocation by integrating the filter predicate into the scoring loop, or collect only once and reuse. Enemy counts are low enough that this is minor, but the allocation is avoidable.

findings.description: combined_haste is always wrapped in Some(f32) via Some(haste_modifier.map(...).unwrap_or(0.0) + enrage_state.speed_bonus). The Option adds no information since calculate_weighted_movement treats None and Some(0.0) identically.
findings.recommendation: Compute combined_haste as a plain f32 and pass Some(combined_haste) explicitly, or restructure the helper signature to accept f32 for this parameter.

findings.description: lich_movement contains two nearly identical steering-physics blocks for the Approaching and Combat phases. Both compute max_speed, apply STEERING_FORCE-clamped acceleration, set velocity.max_speed, and apply VELOCITY_DAMPING. Only the target direction vector differs.
findings.recommendation: Extract a private apply_steering(velocity, acceleration, target_dir, max_speed, delta) helper and call it from both branches to eliminate the duplication.

findings.description: update_lich_targeting unconditionally collects all_units into a Vec<_> heap allocation every frame, even when the Lich is in Approaching or Summoning phase where the snapshot is immediately discarded after the phase != LichPhase::Combat check.
findings.recommendation: Add an early-return guard: if none of the lich entities is in LichPhase::Combat, skip building the snapshot entirely.

findings.description: lich_combat_targeting builds non_king: Vec<Entity> and eligible: Vec<Entity> every frame, even during the long BEAM_COOLDOWN window when fod.target.is_some() or !fod.is_ready() causes the inner loop to immediately continue. The defender collection loop over all non-corpse non-boss units runs before the readiness check.
findings.recommendation: Check fod.target.is_some() || !fod.is_ready() before the defender collection loop; use continue to skip the heap allocation during the cooldown window.

findings.description: BruteAssets is an empty stub resource that is registered at startup in brute/plugin.rs:14 but never consumed by any system. spawn_brute takes Res<InfantryAssets>, not Res<BruteAssets>. The startup system preload_brute_assets only calls commands.insert_resource(BruteAssets) — a zero-byte resource with no fields.
findings.recommendation: Delete BruteAssets, preload_brute_assets, and the Startup system registration in BrutePlugin. Restore when brute gets its own sprite assets.

findings.description: spawn_stat_row, spawn_stat_text_row, spawn_stat_value_row in endless_tab.rs are near-identical duplicates of the same helpers in src/ui/compendium/rows.rs (and a third copy exists in pause_menu). Three diverging copies of the same label+value row pattern.
findings.recommendation: Promote a canonical spawn_stat_value_row + wrappers to src/ui/layout_helpers.rs with pub(crate) visibility (coordinate with ui-root owner), then remove the local copies from endless_tab.rs.

findings.description: TutorialProgress::is_completed allocates a String via tutorial.id().to_string() on every call and performs an O(n) linear scan on Vec<String>. mark_completed has the same allocation pattern. Called on every trigger invocation.
findings.recommendation: Change completed to HashSet<String> for O(1) lookup, or compare using self.completed.iter().any(|c| c == id) where id: &str to avoid allocations.

findings.description: The 'Got it' / 'Next' label logic is duplicated between spawn_tutorial_overlay (line 344-347) and update_tutorial_content (line 737-740). If the wording changes, both sites must be updated.
findings.recommendation: Extract fn next_button_label(step: usize, total: usize) -> &'static str and call it from both sites.

findings.description: The doc comment on trigger_kbm_menus_tutorial says 'Mirrors the controller variant' but no controller-specific menus tutorial variant exists anywhere in the codebase. The comment is a leftover from a planned feature.
findings.recommendation: Update the comment to remove the reference to a non-existent controller variant, or note that the gamepad path is intentionally absent.

findings.description: let count = 0u32; in update_lensing_positions is a dead variable. Slots 0-1 were previously used for black-hole lensing and are now permanently zeroed. The variable is only used in the max_slot fallback expression and contributes no behavior.
findings.recommendation: Replace the variable with an inline literal (0u32) in the max_slot expression and update the comment to note that slots 0-1 are permanently unused, or remove the variable entirely if lensing will never be restored.

findings.description: Module-level comment 'Bindings are hardcoded here for now; rebinding UI lives in a later phase' is stale — controller rebinding Phase 1+2 was delivered at v0.6.286 per project history, and the gamepad action bindings here remain hardcoded with no known plan to add them to the config system.
findings.recommendation: Update the comment to note these gamepad action bindings are intentionally hardcoded and do not participate in the config-based rebinding system, or remove the forward-looking reference entirely.

findings.description: animate_fortified_horde_glow contains an early-out if shielded.is_empty() guard that is redundant because the system is already gated by .run_if(any_exist::<FortifiedHordeShield>()) in the plugin.
findings.recommendation: Remove the if shielded.is_empty() guard inside the system body and rely solely on the run_if condition.

findings.description: In tear_down_socket, a poisoned-Mutex branch silently skips taking the ListenSocket (if let Ok(...) = socket.listener.lock() with no else). A Mutex poison occurs when a lock-holder panicked — possible in tests or future refactors.
findings.recommendation: Add an else arm: `} else { warn!("[Steam MP] ListenSocket Mutex poisoned — listener not dropped"); }`. Same pattern at line 57.

findings.description: The peer field in SteamLobbyState::Joined is suppressed with #[allow(dead_code)], but sync_coop_peer_name in lobby_systems.rs already reads it via client.friends().get_friend(peer).name(). The attribute is stale doc drift.
findings.recommendation: Remove #[allow(dead_code)] — the field is live.

findings.description: Comment references `networking_types.rs:1879` in the upstream bevy_steamworks crate. That line number will silently stale on any crate version bump.
findings.recommendation: Replace the line-number reference with a prose explanation of the invariant (the Steam API merges all send-flag variants on receive, so a prefix tag byte is used instead).

findings.description: TransportEvent::PingUpdate(f32) is #[allow(dead_code)] — the iroh transport never emits it. The bridge handler at bridge.rs:162-164 processes an event that is never sent.
findings.recommendation: Either implement ping measurement on the iroh connection path and emit PingUpdate, or remove the variant and its dead bridge handler.

findings.description: toggle_debug_ui_visible is registered in Update with no run_if guard. Every other Update system in the project carries an explicit run condition, making this an outlier.
findings.recommendation: Add a lightweight guard such as .run_if(not(in_state(AppState::Loading))) to match project convention.

findings.description: fire.rs is 739 LOC and contains at least four distinct sub-concerns: per-gun entry point firing functions, hitscan ray spawn + collision, bullet tracer movement + cleanup, and flame particle lifecycle + VFX emission. Exceeds the 300-LOC guideline with multiple separable concerns.
findings.recommendation: Split into hitscan.rs (ray spawn + check_hitscan_collisions), tracer.rs (spawn_tracer + move_tracers + despawn_distant_tracers), flamethrower.rs (FlameParticle systems + FlameGroundFire), keeping fire.rs as the per-gun entry-point functions.

findings.description: TalentDefinition.implemented: bool is marked #[allow(dead_code)], is never set to false anywhere in the codebase, and is never read. It results in 279 literal 'implemented: true' entries that carry no information.
findings.recommendation: Remove the field and all 'implemented: true' literals to eliminate the dead_code suppression and reduce noise.

findings.description: Doc comments on SaveConfigMessage (line 3) and ConfigChanged (line 13) refer to 'localStorage'. Same stale reference in progress.rs:149 and save_data.rs:36. The game is native-only and writes to %APPDATA%/court_wizard/.
findings.recommendation: Replace all four 'localStorage' references with 'disk' or 'the save directory'.

findings.description: tick_dimensional_rift is a full Bevy system defined in arrival.rs but has no arrival-phase responsibility — it ticks an ongoing persistent portal. It belongs in a rift.rs or should be re-exported cleanly.
findings.recommendation: Move tick_dimensional_rift to a new rift.rs sibling file as part of splitting arrival.rs.

findings.description: Doc comment on font_of_life_detect_deaths reads '/// Computes talent parameters from active talent selections.' — same wrong boilerplate. The function scans new corpses inside Font-of-Life zones and tags them for resurrection.
findings.recommendation: Replace with '/// Scans new corpses inside Font-of-Life zones and tags them for resurrection.'

findings.description: Two .expect("checked above") calls in tick_eye_transfer (lines 801 and 854) rely on an invariant that needs_flight is only true when the source Option is Some. The invariant holds now but is fragile under refactoring — it reads as a hidden panic path rather than a type-enforced guarantee.
findings.recommendation: Restructure using inner if let bindings to extract the source entity, eliminating the .expect calls and making the logic self-documenting.

findings.description: hag_separation allocates a Vec<(Entity, Vec3)> snapshot of all hag positions every frame the system runs, even when no hags are within separation range. With only 3 hags the cost is trivial but is inconsistent with the codebase pattern of avoiding per-frame allocations.
findings.recommendation: Iterate directly over hags using two nested loops (skipping same entity), eliminating the snapshot Vec.

findings.description: The doc comment '/// Attenuated volume for Ray's sound effects — slight falloff from wizard/camera position.' sits directly above ray_mind_control_beam (line 28) but describes ray_sfx_volume, which lives in movement.rs. The comment was left behind when ray_sfx_volume was moved.
findings.recommendation: Delete the orphaned comment from beams.rs:26-27.

findings.description: ray_teleport_eye calls materials.add(StandardMaterial { ... }) each time the teleport fires (cooldown 15 s). The bubble material is stateless and identical every time, so this is an avoidable runtime asset allocation.
findings.recommendation: Add a bubble_material: Handle<StandardMaterial> field to RayAssets and create it in preload_ray_assets, eliminating the runtime allocation.

findings.description: ogre_charge_system has the doc comment '/// Spawns the ogre at one of the tunnel spawn points.' — copied verbatim from spawn_ogre and never updated. The function is the charge state machine driver.
findings.recommendation: Replace with an accurate description of the charge state machine (idle cooldown, targeting, telegraphing, charging, recovery).

findings.description: spawn_arrow carries the doc comment 'Updates archer movement timers to track time since stopped moving.' — a copy-paste from update_archer_movement_timers. The function actually spawns a ballistic arrow entity.
findings.recommendation: Replace with an accurate doc comment, e.g. 'Spawns a ballistic arrow entity from origin toward target for the given team.'

findings.description: update_archer_targeting has the doc comment 'Updates archer movement timers to track time since stopped moving.' — the same wrong copy-paste. The function sets each archer's targeting velocity toward the nearest enemy in range.
findings.recommendation: Replace with an accurate doc comment, e.g. 'Sets each archer's targeting velocity toward the nearest enemy within attack range, accounting for LOS and wall proximity.'

findings.description: check_arrow_collisions performs a two-step redundant same-team check: first `if *team == arrow.source_team { continue }` then immediately after `let is_enemy = ...; if !is_enemy { continue }`. The first check is fully subsumed by the second (is_enemy already returns false for the source team).
findings.recommendation: Remove the explicit `if *team == arrow.source_team { continue }` check and rely solely on `is_enemy`.

findings.description: ParchmentPanel and FrostedGlassOverlay marker components are defined in button_systems.rs but are semantically owned by layout_helpers.rs, which defines the ParchmentMaterial/FrostedGlassMaterial types and the apply_* systems that consume these markers. A reader of layout_helpers.rs must hunt in button_systems.rs to find the markers for materials defined there.
findings.recommendation: Move ParchmentPanel and FrostedGlassOverlay definitions to layout_helpers.rs alongside the material types they gate, and remove them from button_systems.rs.

findings.description: The file-level doc comment says 'Study tab detail panels, sliders, talent cards, cursor systems.' The word 'panels' is misleading — UI panel spawning lives in panels.rs, not here. This was likely copied during the file split (Phase 16 per mod.rs) and never corrected.
findings.recommendation: Update the module docstring: 'Study tab detail panel interaction — slider drag, talent click/hover, allocation text refresh, gamepad cursor.'

findings.description: The doc comment on handle_confirmation_popup (lines 19-25) is a verbatim copy-paste of the setup function's doc comment from builders.rs: 'Sets up the settings menu UI with a tabbed interface. Creates a settings screen with tabs for Graphics, Audio, Game, and Controls. Tab content is rebuilt dynamically...' This is entirely wrong for a confirmation-popup handler.
findings.recommendation: Replace with a correct doc: '/// Handles confirmation popup button clicks and gamepad Back presses.'

findings.description: update_slider_text formats all slider values as '{}%', (value * 100.0) as u8. For sliders with ranges outside [0,1] this produces misleading output: GameSpeed at its minimum (0.5) shows '50%', at maximum (2.0) shows '200%'; UiBrightness max shows '200%'; GamepadResponseCurve max shows '350%'. Players see '200%' for max brightness.
findings.recommendation: Add a display_text(value: f32) -> String method to SliderValue that returns values in appropriate units (e.g. 'x2.0' for GameSpeed, raw decimal for deadzone, '200%' only for volume sliders).

findings.description: _wt_buttons: Query<(Entity, &WizardTowerButtonAction), Without<TutorialHighlightable>> is declared but never iterated. Bevy still resolves this query every frame ActiveTutorial exists. The StartBattleButton and TimeTravelButton HighlightTarget variants are referenced only in deprecated step arrays and are never tagged.
findings.recommendation: Remove the dead _wt_buttons parameter and the unused WizardTowerButtonAction import from tag_wizard_tower_entities.

findings.description: nearest_in_direction materialises its IntoIterator argument into a Vec<(Entity, Vec2)> unconditionally on every focus navigation frame (line 76), even though the horizontal-nav single-pass path iterates it only once.
findings.recommendation: Remove the unconditional collect(); iterate the IntoIterator directly in the horizontal-nav branch. Only collect for the vertical two-pass branch that needs a slice reference.

findings.description: NotificationQueue::pop uses Vec::remove(0), an O(n) front-removal that shifts all remaining entries. Notification bursts (e.g., unlocking a wizard triggering ingredient/spell/talent toasts) make this worst-case linear.
findings.recommendation: Replace Vec<NotificationEntry> with std::collections::VecDeque<NotificationEntry> and change remove(0) to pop_front().

findings.description: DEFENDER_RALLY_DELAY_SECS is defined at line 348, well after its only use at line 212. All other constants in this codebase are placed near the top of the file or alongside the code that owns them.
findings.recommendation: Move the constant to the top of runtime.rs (or to a future rebuild.rs) alongside other staging-related constants.

findings.description: IngredientDrop::time_alive is documented as 'for despawn and fade' but no fade or timeout-despawn logic exists in the drops module. The field is used only for animation (bobbing and pulse math).
findings.recommendation: Update the field doc to 'for animation (bobbing and pulse)'. If timed despawn/fade is desired, add a DROP_MAX_LIFETIME constant and a despawn branch inside tick_drop_lifetimes.

findings.description: toggle_diagnostics runs unconditionally every Update frame with no run_if guard, polling keyboard input even when diagnostics are already disabled. Violates the project's every-Update-system-needs-run_if convention, though it is gated behind the benchmarking feature flag.
findings.recommendation: Add a run_if guard (e.g., resource_equals or a not(diagnostics_enabled) condition) or accept the early-return pattern given the feature-flag gating — the cost is negligible but the pattern inconsistency is worth flagging.

findings.description: The pure-math geometry methods contains_point_with_radius, intersects_hitbox_cylinder, and eclipse_geometry implement non-trivial spatial math with cone projections, XZ flattening (ground_collision mode), ellipse clipping, and multiple edge cases. None have unit tests. These are high-churn collision primitives shared by wizard beams, crystal beams, and terrain hit-testing.
findings.recommendation: Add #[cfg(test)] unit tests covering: point at origin (returns false), point at tip (returns true), lateral miss, cone growth at t=0.5, ground_collision XZ flattening, and eclipse_geometry range clipping.

findings.description: init.rs at 391 lines crosses the 300-line guideline and mixes three distinct concerns: (1) co-op session promotion and handshake setup (lines 43-67), (2) queue population for world/terrain/units, and (3) resource initialization for WaveState, RetreatState, and InitialDefenderCount. These concerns could be isolated for readability.
findings.recommendation: Extract co-op session promotion into coop_session.rs (or inline into init.rs with a clearly marked section), and extract WaveState/RetreatState initialization into a wave_init.rs helper called from init_loading_progress. Keep terrain + unit enqueue in init.rs.

findings.description: combat.rs is 619 LOC mixing avatar physics helpers (apply_avatar_physics, spawn_avatar_missile), input-driven systems (player_movement, fire_missile, sword_swing), sword arc VFX (build_arc_strip_mesh, spawn_sword_arc, update_sword_arcs), and retreat/state logic. Multiple distinct concerns exceed the 300-LOC guideline.
findings.recommendation: Split into avatar_movement.rs (physics helper + player_movement), sword_arc.rs (mesh building + spawn_sword_arc + update_sword_arcs), and keep combat.rs for spawn_avatar_missile + retreat/block logic.

findings.description: cast_effects.rs (690 LOC) absorbs the entire MP-sync wrapper layer (emit_cast_event, spawn_school_flare_synced, spawn_aura_bubble_synced, spawn_smoke_poof_synced, spawn_floating_motes_synced, spawn_sparks_with_material_synced, spawn_dust_smoke_synced, emit_banishment_lens_event — ~220 lines). These are a distinct concern from local VFX spawning.
findings.recommendation: Split into cast_effects.rs (local spawners + updaters) and mp_sync.rs (all *_synced wrappers + emit_cast_event). Matches CLAUDE.md group-by-concern rule and brings both files under 300 LOC.

findings.description: `collapsing_wall_explosion` performs a full `O(walls × enemies)` nested loop scan every `PostCombatSet` tick while any `WallTalents` entity exists, including frames where no wall is dead or sinking.
findings.recommendation: Use an observer/trigger on health reaching zero, or gate the inner enemy scan behind an early-continue when `!health.is_dead() || !wall.sinking`. Add a comment documenting the performance bound.

findings.description: casting.rs is 532 LOC and bundles casting input handling, storm spawning logic, projectile entity factory (spawn_meteor_projectile_entity), and explosion entity factory (spawn_explosion_entity). Factory functions that create projectile/explosion entities belong alongside those entities' systems rather than in the casting input file.
findings.recommendation: As part of the meteor.rs split (see F2), extract spawn_meteor_projectile_entity, MeteorProjectileTalentFlags, and spawn_explosion_entity into projectile.rs, reducing casting.rs to ~350 LOC focused purely on input and storm spawning.

findings.description: check_wave_activation contains the 90%-threshold, timeout force-activation, and swordcerer-aggro early activation logic — the most game-play-critical wave-progression code in the module. No tests cover the threshold boundary, timeout path, or aggro-activation branch.
findings.recommendation: Extract the threshold/activation decision into a pure function and add unit tests covering: exactly 90% arrived, just under 90%, timeout expiry, and avatar proximity aggro.

findings.description: sync_trampling_texture rebuilds a 360,000-cell (1.44 MB) pixel buffer every dirty sync (up to 4x/s). The Vec::with_capacity + per-cell push loop + Image::new + images.remove + images.add cycle is avoidable allocation pressure given the grid is sparsely dirty in practice.
findings.recommendation: Maintain a persistent reusable Vec<u8> and write into it in-place across syncs to avoid repeated heap allocation. Dirty-rectangle tracking could further limit per-sync work to only changed cells.

findings.description: update_fire_glow and update_missile_glow (explosion_effects.rs:110) are structurally identical: track source Transform, apply pulsing scale using constants. cleanup_orphaned_glows and cleanup_orphaned_missile_glows are also identical. Four near-duplicate functions totalling ~60 lines differing only in component type and 3 constants.
findings.recommendation: Introduce generic helpers update_tracking_glow::<G> and cleanup_orphaned_glow::<G> parameterized over a trait or const generics carrying the size multiplier, pulse frequency, and pulse amplitude. Reduces 4 functions to 2 generic + 2 small instantiations.

findings.description: MpPauseSettingsPlugin and PauseSettingsPlugin are structurally identical: same imported systems, same Update batches, same ButtonActionSet grouping, identical debug-assertions block. They differ only in the Back-action destination state. All shared Update systems are registered twice independently.
findings.recommendation: Extract a shared registration function that takes the state variant, deduplicating the ~50 duplicated registration lines. Keep only the Back-action system state-specific.

findings.description: update_lightning_bolts calls despawn_related::<Children>() and re-spawns 20-30 child quad entities every frame per active bolt for the crackle animation. At 10+ simultaneous chain-lightning bolts this is 200-300 entity spawn/despawn operations per frame. The design is intentional but scales poorly with bolt count.
findings.recommendation: Consider pre-allocating a fixed pool of child quad entities per bolt and updating their Transforms each frame instead of destroying and recreating. Flag as a future optimization; not blocking current gameplay.

findings.description: check_roguelite_modifier_achievements is the most complex system in the module (~130 LOC, multiple tuple params, float near() comparisons, combo condition ordering). A logic error in the modifier value thresholds or combo detection would silently fail to unlock achievements with no test coverage.
findings.recommendation: Extract the condition logic (near() comparisons, combo detection) into pure functions accepting f32 values and returning which achievements should unlock. These can be unit-tested without Bevy's ECS harness.

apply_wizard_stats_to_primed_spell and reset_empowerment_after_cast both query With<Wizard> and would match GuestWizard. Does the GuestWizard entity have PrimedSpell inserted on the host? If so, is the empowerment reset lifecycle correct for the host-driven (message-based) guest cast flow?

Is the Psychopath archetype intentionally disabled for multiplayer permanently, or just deferred? The plugin only hooks AppState::InGame; a comment or explicit run_if(!is_multiplayer) guard would make intent clear.

The drain-and-requeue pattern in swordcerer/networking.rs and meteorologist/networking.rs is informal protocol multiplexing. Is there a plan to centralize message routing, or is ad-hoc drain acceptable long-term as the network protocol grows?
Is Spell::Fireball => [1, 2, 3] intentional? It unlocks all three talent tiers on the very first battle while every other damage spell requires tens to thousands of uses.
Is the TalentDefinition.implemented field still serving any undocumented purpose (e.g. driving a UI lock state that was removed), or is it fully orphaned?
Are set_selection and has_talent on ActiveTalents placeholders for a planned talent-selection UI flow, or can they be removed?
